definition_zh: 通信往来；往来书信；相似性；对应关系
definition_en: the exchange of letters or messages between people, or a close similarity or matching relation between two things
core_image: 两叠信纸分别排成两列，每一页都正对着另一页

senses.title: The exchange of letters
senses.titleCN: 通信往来：一来一回的信
senses.definition: the act of writing letters or messages to someone and receiving theirs
senses.definitionCN: 向某人写信或发消息并收到其回信的行为
senses.example: Their correspondence lasted for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的通信持续了四十年。
senses.why: correspondere joins com- 'together' with respondere 'to answer': two sides answer each other, and -ence names the ongoing state of that answering.
senses.whyCN: correspondere 由 com-“一起”与 respondere“回答”组成：两边互相回信，-ence 指出的正是这种回应的持续状态。

senses.title: A body of letters
senses.titleCN: 信件本身：收起来的一整套往来书信
senses.definition: the letters or emails themselves, considered as a collection
senses.definitionCN: 被当作一个集合来看的往来信件或邮件本身
senses.example: Her correspondence with the poet is now kept in the national library.
senses.exampleCN: 她与那位诗人的往来书信如今保存在国家图书馆。
senses.why: The -ence noun can name a mass as well as an activity, so the same word shifts from the act of answering to the pile of sheets that carries the answers.
senses.whyCN: -ence 名词既能指活动，也能指一堆事物，因此这个词从“回信这一行为”滑向“承载回信的那叠纸”。

senses.title: Similarity between two things
senses.titleCN: 相似性：两样东西彼此对得上
senses.definition: a close similarity or analogy between two things
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物之间高度的相似或类比关系
senses.example: There is a striking correspondence between the two maps.
senses.exampleCN: 这两幅地图之间有惊人的相似性。
senses.why: correspondere first meant 'to answer to or be in harmony with'. Two things that answer each other in structure are read as alike, so the noun covers analogy as well as letters.
senses.whyCN: correspondere 最初意为“与……相答、彼此协调”。两样东西在结构上相互应答，就被读成相似，于是这个名词也覆盖了类比义。

senses.title: Agreement with the facts
senses.titleCN: 相符：说法与事实对得上
senses.definition: the degree to which an account, theory or record agrees with the facts
senses.definitionCN: 陈述、理论或记录与事实相符的程度
senses.example: The witness's account shows little correspondence with the physical evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 证人的陈述与物证几乎对不上。
senses.why: When a statement answers the facts correctly, it 'responds' properly; the noun measures how well that answer fits what actually happened.
senses.whyCN: 当陈述正确回应事实时，它才“答得对”；这个名词衡量的正是这一回答与实际发生之事契合得有多好。

senses.title: A one-to-one match
senses.titleCN: 一一对应：左边每一页只配右边一页
senses.definition: in mathematics, a relation in which each element of one set is paired with exactly one element of another
senses.definitionCN: 数学中一个集合的每个元素与另一集合恰好一个元素配对的关系
senses.example: The proof establishes a one-to-one correspondence between the two sets.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明建立了两个集合之间的一一对应。
senses.why: The picture of paired sheets becomes exact in mathematics: every sheet on the left has exactly one partner on the right, with none left over.
senses.whyCN: 配对信纸的画面在数学里变得精确：左边每页恰好配右边一页，没有一页多出来。

senses.title: An official channel
senses.titleCN: 官方通信渠道：机构之间的公文往来
senses.definition: the regular exchange of official letters between institutions or governments
senses.definitionCN: 机构或政府之间定期的公函往来
senses.example: Diplomatic correspondence between the two countries resumed last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 两国之间的外交文书往来去年春天恢复。
senses.why: Institutions answer each other on paper, so the noun names not only the paper but the established channel through which the answers travel.
senses.whyCN: 机构之间用纸面互相答复，因此这个名词不只指纸，也指答复往返所经的既定渠道。

senses.title: Business letters
senses.titleCN: 商务函件：买卖双方的书面往来
senses.definition: letters and emails relating to commercial or administrative business
senses.definitionCN: 与商业或行政事务有关的信件和邮件
senses.example: All business correspondence should be filed under the client's name.
senses.exampleCN: 所有商务往来函件都应按客户姓名归档。
senses.why: Commerce runs on written answers to written requests, so the general sense narrows to the professional traffic of offers, orders and complaints.
senses.whyCN: 商业靠书面请求与书面答复运转，于是这个广义词收窄为报价、订单与投诉构成的专业往来。

senses.title: The readers' letters column
senses.titleCN: 读者来信栏：报纸上的公开回信
senses.definition: the section of a newspaper or magazine that prints letters from readers
senses.definitionCN: 报纸或杂志刊登读者来信的栏目
senses.example: Her complaint appeared in the correspondence column of the Sunday paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她的投诉刊登在周日报纸的读者来信栏。
senses.why: A newspaper answers its readers by printing their letters; the column is the public place where those answers appear side by side.
senses.whyCN: 报纸通过刊登读者来信来回应读者；这个栏目就是那些答复并排出现的公开位置。

senses.title: The correspondence theory of truth
senses.titleCN: 真理符合论：真话与实在对得上
senses.definition: in philosophy, the view that a statement is true when it corresponds to reality
senses.definitionCN: 哲学观点：陈述与现实相符时为真
senses.example: The correspondence theory of truth treats facts as the measure of true statements.
senses.exampleCN: 真理符合论把事实当作衡量真陈述的尺度。
senses.why: Philosophy takes the everyday 'agreement with the facts' sense and turns it into a theory: truth is the fit between a statement and the world, like an answer that matches its question.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常“与事实相符”的义项提升为理论：真就是陈述与世界之间的契合，如同答语与问题相配。

intro.en: Correspondence is a Latin-derived noun built on correspond, itself from Medieval Latin correspondere 'to answer together'. The English dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: correspondence 是建立在 correspond 之上的拉丁来源名词，correspond 又来自中世纪拉丁 correspondere“相互回应”。以下英语年代均为大致估计。

items.en: respondere meant 'to answer, promise in return', made of re- 'back' and spondere 'to promise, pledge'. Adding com- 'together' produced correspondere, 'to answer each other, be in harmony'.
items.cn: respondere 意为“回答、回诺”，由 re-“回”与 spondere“许诺、担保”构成。加上 com-“一起”就得到 correspondere，意为“互相应答、彼此协调”。

items.en: The abstract noun correspondentia 'mutual answering' was formed with -ia, the ancestor of English -ence. French correspondance carried it into Middle English.
items.cn: 抽象名词 correspondentia“相互应答”由 -ia 构成，即英语 -ence 的前身；法语 correspondance 把它带入中古英语。

items.en: English correspond appears around the early 15th century with the sense 'be in harmony, answer to'. The date is approximate and the earliest records are legal and religious.
items.cn: 英语 correspond 约在15世纪初出现，意为“相合、与……相应”。年代为约数，最早记录见于法律与宗教文本。

items.en: By the 17th century the verb had also come to mean 'exchange letters', since letters are answers exchanged in writing. The noun then named both the activity and the collected sheets.
items.cn: 到17世纪，这个动词又表示“互通书信”，因为信件正是以书面形式互换的答复。名词于是同时指这一活动和收存起来的信件。

items.en: Mathematics adopted one-to-one correspondence in the 19th century, and philosophy made the correspondence theory of truth a standard label in the 20th. Both extend the same 'answer that fits' image.
items.cn: 数学在19世纪采用 one-to-one correspondence（一一对应），哲学在20世纪把 correspondence theory of truth（真理符合论）变成标准术语。两者都延伸了同一个“答语相合”的意象。

items.en: The deeper origin of Latin spondere is uncertain; it is often connected with a root meaning 'to make an offering', but this is a reconstruction. Exact first dates for the English senses are also uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁 spondere 的更深来源不确定；常被联系到一个意为“献祭、许愿”的词根，但这属于重构。英语各义项的最早确切年代同样存疑。

note.en: The first group contains spelling neighbours that are easily confused with correspondence; the second contains words that share part of its meaning but stress a different side.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 correspondence 混淆的形近词；第二组是共享部分词义、但强调不同侧面的近义词。

entries.definition: A person who writes letters or reports news from a place. It is the human agent, while correspondence is the traffic of letters itself.
entries.definitionCN: 通信者或驻外记者，指人；correspondence 指书信往来的活动或信件本身。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'matching or analogous', or 'relating to letters'. It describes a relation, not the letters as a body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为“相应的、对应的”或“通信的”，描述关系而非成堆的信件。

entries.definition: In older divorce law, the third party accused of misconduct with the respondent. The hyphen and extra sense make it a trap for learners.
entries.definitionCN: 旧离婚法中被指与被告有不当关系的第三方。连字符与额外义项使它成为易混陷阱。

entries.definition: The general exchange of information by any means; correspondence is the narrower, letter-based form.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何方式交换信息的统称；correspondence 是更窄的书信形式。

entries.definition: The letters and parcels themselves as physical items; it does not carry the idea of a continuing two-way relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 作为实物的信件与包裹；它不包含持续双向关系之意。

entries.definition: A similarity in structure used to explain something; it overlaps correspondence sense 3 but is usually an explanatory tool.
entries.definitionCN: 用于解释事物的结构相似；对应第 3 个义项，但通常是一种解释工具。

entries.definition: A close likeness between two developments or sets; it stresses running alongside rather than answering each other.
entries.definitionCN: 两个发展或集合之间的高度相似；强调并排而行，而非彼此应答。

entries.definition: Agreement among statements or parts of a whole; closer to sense 4 than to the letter sense.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述之间或整体各部分之间的一致性；更接近第 4 个义项，而非书信义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'together' + respondere 'answer': two people answer together, one letter after another.
normal.cn: com-“一起”+ respondere“回答”：两个人一起应答，一封接一封地写信。

normal.en: The -ence ending makes a noun of state, so correspondence is the state of answering each other.
normal.cn: -ence 结尾构成状态名词，所以 correspondence 就是“彼此回应”的状态。

normal.en: Standard collocations are keep up a correspondence, business correspondence and one-to-one correspondence; they show the three main senses.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 keep up a correspondence、business correspondence、one-to-one correspondence，正好展示三个主要义项。

normal.en: correspond, correspondent, corresponding, correspondingly and correspondence share the same respond- stem.
normal.cn: correspond、correspondent、corresponding、correspondingly、correspondence 共享同一个 respond- 词干。

normal.en: correspondent is the person; correspondence is the letters. Keeping that pair apart prevents a common writing error.
normal.cn: correspondent 是人，correspondence 是信；把这组区分开可避免常见写作错误。

abstract.en: Picture two columns of letters facing each other across a table, each line answered by the line opposite.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两列信纸遥遥相对，每一行都被对面那一行回应。

abstract.en: Picture two sets of keys laid out so that every key on the left opens exactly one lock on the right.
abstract.cn: 想象两排钥匙摆开，左边每把恰好开右边一把锁。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger line and a receipt line adding up to the same figure: that is correspondence between account and fact.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿一行与收据一行加总为同一个数字：这就是账与事实的相符。

examples.en: The archive contains the correspondence between the two scientists from 1930 to 1955.
examples.cn: 档案馆收藏了这两位科学家 1930 至 1955 年间的往来书信。

examples.en: There is little correspondence between what the advertisement promises and what the product does.
examples.cn: 广告承诺与产品实际功能之间几乎没有相符之处。

examples.en: The study found a correspondence between rising temperatures and earlier flowering dates.
examples.cn: 研究发现了气温上升与开花日期提前之间的对应关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: “可（cor）respond 应（ence）”——你一回我一应，信纸排成对 → correspondence 通信往来、对应关系

root: 拉丁 correspondere“相互回应、彼此相合”（com-“一起”+ respondere“回答”，其中 re-“回”+ spondere“许诺”）；correspond + -ence 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses branch from one gesture: one thing answers another. Letters answer letters, facts answer statements, and sets pair off sheet by sheet.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个动作分叉：一物回应另一物。信回应信，事实回应陈述，集合则一页对一页地配对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two columns of sheets, each line answered by the line opposite.
core.cn: 核心意象：两列信纸，每一行都被对面那一行回应。

branches.en: LETTERS: the activity of answering by post and the collected sheets that carry those answers.
branches.cn: 书信：通过邮路相互应答的活动，以及承载这些答复的成叠信件。

branches.en: LIKENESS AND TRUTH: analogy is structural answering, and the correspondence theory makes truth a fit between statement and world.
branches.cn: 相似与真理：类比是结构上的应答，符合论则把真理解为陈述与世界相合。

branches.en: PRACTICAL AGREEMENT: an account that matches the facts and a business letter that answers a request both depend on things lining up.
branches.cn: 实际相符：与事实对得上的陈述、回应请求的商务函件，都依赖两边对齐。

branches.en: MATCHED SETS: mathematical pairing and a newspaper's letters column both place each item beside its partner.
branches.cn: 配对集合：数学配对与报纸来信栏，都把每一项摆在它的对应项旁边。

branches.en: OFFICIAL CHANNEL: institutions answer each other on paper, so the noun also names the route those answers travel.
branches.cn: 官方渠道：机构以纸面互相答复，因此该名词也指这些答复所走的路线。

intro.en: Correspondence is correspondence built on the Latin verb correspondere plus the noun suffix -ence. The prefix com- and the base spondere are fossilized inside the verb, while -ence remains a live English noun ending.
intro.cn: correspondence 是在拉丁动词 correspondere 上加名词后缀 -ence 构成的。前缀 com- 与词基 spondere 已凝固在动词内部，而 -ence 仍是活的英语名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin spondere 'to promise' and respondere 'to answer' supply a family that includes sponsor, spouse, response, responsible, despondent and correspondence. English borrowed these stems at different periods, so the root appears as spond-, spons- and respond-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spondere“许诺”与 respondere“回答”衍生出 sponsor、spouse、response、responsible、despondent、correspondence 等词族。英语在不同时期借入这些词干，因此词根呈现 spond-、spons-、respond- 等形态。

items.meaning: the state of answering each other; letters exchanged
items.meaningCN: 相互回应的状态；往来书信（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: The correspondence between the two offices is kept for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 两个办公室之间的往来函件保存十年。

items.meaning: to exchange letters; to match or agree
items.meaningCN: 通信；相符；对应（com-“一起”+ respondere“回答”）
items.example: The two descriptions do not correspond in every detail.
items.exampleCN: 这两份描述并非每个细节都相符。

items.meaning: a person who writes letters or reports news
items.meaningCN: 通信者；驻外记者（-ent 构成施事名词）
items.example: Our correspondent in Beirut sent the report.
items.exampleCN: 我们驻贝鲁特的记者发回了报道。

items.meaning: matching, analogous, or relating to letters
items.meaningCN: 相应的；通信的（-ing 构成分词形容词）
items.example: Sales rose, with a corresponding fall in unsold stock.
items.exampleCN: 销量上升，未售库存相应下降。

items.meaningCN: 回答；作出反应（re-“回”+ spondere“许诺”）
items.example: She responded to the question without hesitation.
items.exampleCN: 她毫不犹豫地回答了问题。

items.meaningCN: 回答；反应（respons- 词干 + 名词词尾）
items.example: The survey received more than a thousand responses.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查收到了一千多份回复。

items.meaningCN: 有责任的；可靠的（-ible 表示“能够被……的”）
items.example: The officer responsible for the file signed the letter.
items.exampleCN: 负责该档案的官员签署了这封信。

items.meaning: a person or firm that pledges support
items.meaningCN: 赞助者；担保人（spons-“许诺”+ -or 施事后缀）
items.example: The bank agreed to sponsor the exhibition.
items.exampleCN: 银行同意赞助这次展览。

items.meaning: having lost hope, as if a promise was withdrawn
items.meaningCN: 沮丧的；失去希望的（de-“离开”+ spond-“许诺”+ -ent）
items.example: He grew despondent after the third rejection.
items.exampleCN: 第三次被拒后他变得沮丧。

latinEntries.meaning: to answer each other, be in harmony

latinEntries.meaningCN: 相互应答或相符（中世纪拉丁）

definition_zh: 相应的；对应的；相符的；通信的
definition_en: matching or analogous to something else, or relating to written communication
core_image: 两块形状相同的拼图隔着桌面遥遥相对
scene: Each increase in temperature produced a corresponding rise in pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 corresponding 是「相应的」（第 3 个义项：随另一变化同步出现）；句意：温度每升高一次，压力就出现相应的上升。图中可辨识物件：温度计、压力表、上升箭头、数据曲线、实验台。

pos.zh: 相应的；对应的；相符的；通信的（作定语或表语）

collocations.zh: 通讯作者（论文中负责联络的作者）
通讯会员；外籍（非驻会）会员

derivatives.zh: 通信者；驻外记者；相符的
（旧离婚法中的）共同被告（第三方）

senses.title: Matching in shape or position
senses.titleCN: 形状位置相配：左右对得上
senses.definition: having the same shape, size or relative position as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物具有相同的形状、大小或相对位置
senses.example: The corresponding sides of the two triangles are equal.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个三角形的对应边相等。
senses.why: corresponding is the present participle of correspond turned adjective: the two sides answer each other in form, so each is the corresponding one of the other.
senses.whyCN: corresponding 是 correspond 的现在分词转为形容词：两边在形状上相互应答，所以每一边都是另一边的对应者。

senses.title: Analogous in function
senses.titleCN: 功能相当：不同系统里的同一个位置
senses.definition: playing an equivalent role in a different system or organization
senses.definitionCN: 在不同系统或机构中承担相当的角色
senses.example: The corresponding department in the French ministry rejected the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 法国部里对应的部门否决了该计划。
senses.why: The pairing need not be physical: two offices can answer each other functionally, so the adjective extends from shapes to roles.
senses.whyCN: 配对不必是物理的：两个部门可以在功能上相互应答，于是这个形容词从形状延伸到角色。

senses.title: Changing together
senses.titleCN: 同步变化：一边动，另一边跟着动
senses.definition: occurring or changing in step with another change
senses.definitionCN: 与另一变化同步发生或变化
senses.example: Each increase in temperature produced a corresponding rise in pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 温度每升高一次，压力就出现相应的上升。
senses.why: When two quantities answer each other's movement, the change in one is described as corresponding to the change in the other; the adjective marks that matched movement.
senses.whyCN: 当两个量彼此呼应地变动，一个的变化就被描述为与另一个的变化 corresponding；形容词标记的正是这种同步运动。

senses.title: The equivalent item
senses.titleCN: 对等条目：另一份清单里的那一项
senses.definition: the item in another list, table or set that occupies the same place
senses.definitionCN: 在另一清单、表格或集合中处于同一位置的条目
senses.example: Write the corresponding entry in the second column.
senses.exampleCN: 请在第二列写下对应的条目。
senses.why: A column of entries answers another column line by line, so one entry is called corresponding to its partner rather than merely similar to it.
senses.whyCN: 一列条目逐行回应另一列，因此某一项被称为与其搭档 corresponding，而不只是“相似”。

senses.title: Relating to letters
senses.titleCN: 通信的：与书信有关的
senses.definition: relating to the writing and sending of letters
senses.definitionCN: 与写信、寄信有关的
senses.example: Please send all corresponding documents to the registrar.
senses.exampleCN: 请将所有通信文件寄给注册处。
senses.why: The literal verb sense 'to exchange letters' survives in the participial adjective, which can label the documents that belong to that exchange.
senses.whyCN: 动词“互通书信”的本义在分词形容词中保留下来，可用来标记属于该往来的文件。

senses.title: Currently exchanging letters
senses.titleCN: 正在通信的：双方保持书信联系
senses.definition: in the state of exchanging letters with someone
senses.definitionCN: 处于与某人通信的状态
senses.example: The two scholars, corresponding for years, finally met in Rome.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位通信多年的学者终于在罗马见面。
senses.why: Here the -ing form keeps its verbal force: it describes an activity in progress, with the adjective merely attaching that activity to the subject.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ing 形式保留动词力量：它描述进行中的活动，形容词只是把这一活动附着到主语上。

senses.title: Corresponding angles in geometry
senses.titleCN: 几何中的同位角：截线同一侧的同位角
senses.definition: in geometry, angles in the same relative position where a line crosses two others
senses.definitionCN: 几何中一条截线穿过两条线时处于相同相对位置的角
senses.example: When the lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.
senses.exampleCN: 当两条线平行时，同位角相等。
senses.why: Geometry borrowed the everyday 'answering position' sense: the two angles occupy answering corners, so they are called corresponding angles.
senses.whyCN: 几何借用了日常“相应位置”的义项：两个角占据相互应答的角落，因此被称为同位角。

senses.title: A non-resident academic title
senses.titleCN: 通讯会员：不驻会却保持往来的会员
senses.definition: in learned societies, a member who does not attend in person but keeps up formal contact
senses.definitionCN: 在学术团体中不亲自驻会、但保持正式联系的会员
senses.example: He was elected a corresponding member of the academy in 1890.
senses.exampleCN: 1890 年他当选为该学会的通讯会员。
senses.why: The title is literal: such a member corresponds with the society by letter instead of attending meetings, so 'corresponding' names the mode of membership.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔是字面义的：这类会员以书信与学会联系而不出席会议，所以 corresponding 指明的正是会员身份的联系方式。

intro.en: Corresponding is the participial adjective of correspond, from Medieval Latin correspondere. The English dating of the adjective is approximate.
intro.cn: corresponding 是 correspond 的分词形容词，correspond 来自中世纪拉丁 correspondere。该形容词的英语年代为约数。

items.en: correspondere 'to answer each other, be in harmony' combines com- 'together' and respondere 'to answer'. Its parts are transparent only to Latin, not to modern English speakers.
items.cn: correspondere“相互应答、彼此相合”由 com-“一起”与 respondere“回答”组合而成。其内部结构只对拉丁语透明，现代英语使用者已不直接感知。

items.en: The Old English participial ending -ende was replaced in Middle English by -ing from the verbal noun. By the modern period -ing freely makes adjectives of ongoing or characteristic state.
items.cn: 古英语分词词尾 -ende 在中古英语被来自动名词的 -ing 取代。到近代，-ing 可自由构成表示进行或典型状态的形容词。

items.en: From the 17th century, corresponding appears as a bare adjective before nouns such as parts, numbers and offices. The pattern 'the corresponding X' means 'the X that answers the other X'.
items.cn: 从17世纪起，corresponding 作为纯形容词出现在 parts、numbers、offices 等名词前。the corresponding X 的模式意为“与另一 X 相对应的那个 X”。

items.en: Euclidean geometry fixed the phrase corresponding angles in the 18th and 19th centuries. The term is a direct metaphor from position: the angles answer each other across a transversal.
items.cn: 欧几里得几何在18、19世纪固定了 corresponding angles（同位角）这一说法。该术语直接来自位置的隐喻：两个角隔着截线相互应答。

items.en: Corresponding member and corresponding author are 19th- and 20th-century institutional labels. Both describe someone who keeps formal contact rather than attending in person.
items.cn: corresponding member 与 corresponding author 是19、20世纪的机构术语，都指以正式联络而非亲自到场维系的角色。

items.en: The exact century in which corresponding became a fully independent adjective is not recorded with certainty. Latin spondere 'to promise' is of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: corresponding 成为完全独立形容词的确切世纪没有可靠记录。拉丁 spondere“许诺”的更深来源存疑。

note.en: The first group is spelling neighbours; the second group contains adjectives that overlap with 'matching' but assign the match differently.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词；第二组是与“相匹配”重叠、但配对方式不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for letters or similarity. Learners often write 'correspondence parts' when they mean corresponding parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指信件或相似性的名词。学习者常把 corresponding parts 错写成 correspondence parts。

entries.definition: A person who writes letters or reports news; it is a noun, while corresponding is an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 写信或报道新闻的人；是名词，而 corresponding 是形容词。

entries.definition: A rare adjective meaning 'answering, corresponding'. It is archaic and should not be used where corresponding will do.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见形容词，意为“应答的、相应的”；已属古旧，能 used corresponding 时不要用它。

entries.definition: Designed to go together in appearance; it stresses visual or material sameness, not structural answering.
entries.definitionCN: 在外观上配套的；强调视觉或材质一致，而非结构上的相互应答。

entries.definition: Similar in function or role though different in origin; closest to sense 2, but more formal and explicit about different origins.
entries.definitionCN: 来源不同但功能或角色相似；最接近第 2 个义项，但更正式，并明示来源不同。

entries.definition: Equal in value, amount or meaning; it asserts equality, while corresponding only asserts paired position.
entries.definitionCN: 在价值、数量或意义上相等；它断言相等，而 corresponding 只断言位置上的配对。

entries.definition: Belonging separately to each of the items already mentioned; it orders possession, not similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 分别属于前面提到的各项；它安排归属次序，而非相似性。

entries.definition: Developing in a similar way at the same time; it stresses simultaneous likeness rather than one-to-one answering.
entries.definitionCN: 同时以相似方式发展；强调同时性的相似，而非一一应答。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, standard collocations and genuine word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、标准搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: correspond + -ing: the -ing ending turns 'answers to' into an adjective that can sit before a noun.
normal.cn: correspond + -ing：-ing 把“与……相应”变成可放在名词前的形容词。

normal.en: The phrase 'the corresponding X' always implies another X already mentioned; the adjective is a pointer, not a description of quality.
normal.cn: the corresponding X 总暗示前面已提到另一个 X；这个形容词是指针，不是性质描写。

normal.en: Learn it with corresponding author, corresponding member and corresponding angles; these are fixed academic uses.
normal.cn: 与 corresponding author、corresponding member、corresponding angles 一起记；这些是固定的学术用法。

normal.en: correspond, correspondence, correspondent and correspondingly all keep the respond- core.
normal.cn: correspond、correspondence、correspondent、correspondingly 都保留 respond- 核心。

normal.en: Do not confuse corresponding (adjective) with correspondence (noun); one describes a match, the other names the match or the letters.
normal.cn: 不要把 corresponding（形容词）与 correspondence（名词）混淆：一个描述匹配，一个命名匹配关系或信件。

abstract.en: Picture two puzzle pieces of the same outline facing each other across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两块轮廓相同的拼图隔着桌子相对。

abstract.en: Picture two dials linked by a rod: turn one and the other moves by the same amount.
abstract.cn: 想象两个表盘由一根连杆相连：转动一个，另一个也移动相同幅度。

abstract.en: Picture two columns of a bilingual dictionary, each line standing level with its translation.
abstract.cn: 想象双语词典的两列，每一行都与它的译文齐平。

examples.en: The report lists each cause and its corresponding effect.
examples.cn: 报告列出每一项原因及其相应的结果。

examples.en: A fall in demand led to a corresponding fall in production.
examples.cn: 需求下降导致了产量的相应下降。

examples.en: The corresponding author is responsible for answering queries about the paper.
examples.cn: 通讯作者负责回答有关该论文的询问。

dict_mnemonic.text: “可（cor）respond 应（ing）”——边回信边对应，左边一页右边一页 → corresponding 相应的、对应的

root: 拉丁 correspondere“相互应答”（com-“一起”+ respondere“回答”，re-“回”+ spondere“许诺”）；correspond + -ing 分词形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one relation: one item answers another, whether in shape, function, timing, list position, geometry or academic correspondence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一种关系：一项回应另一项，无论是在形状、功能、时间、清单位置、几何还是学术通信上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two same-shaped pieces facing each other, each answering the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块同形物件相对而置，彼此应答。

branches.en: FORM AND GEOMETRY: equal sides and corresponding angles are the same positional answer drawn with lines.
branches.cn: 形状与几何：相等的边与同位角，是用线条画出的同一种位置应答。

branches.en: FUNCTION AND TITLE: an office answers another office, and a corresponding member answers the society by letter.
branches.cn: 功能与头衔：一个部门回应另一个部门，通讯会员则以书信回应学会。

branches.en: CHANGE: quantities rise together.
branches.cn: 变化：数值同步上升。

branches.en: LETTERS: documents of the exchange and the people currently exchanging them both belong to written answering.
branches.cn: 书信：往来的文件与正在通信的人，都属于书面应答。

branches.en: EQUIVALENT ITEM: the corresponding entry is the one that occupies the answering slot in another set.
branches.cn: 对等条目：对应条目就是在另一集合中占据应答位置的那一项。

intro.en: Corresponding is correspond plus the participial suffix -ing. The base verb is Latin; the suffix is native English, so the word mixes a borrowed stem with a live English ending.
intro.cn: corresponding 由 correspond 加分词后缀 -ing 构成。词基动词来自拉丁语，后缀是英语本族成分，因此这个词是借入词干与活英语词尾的混合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is spondere 'to promise' with the prefix com-, giving correspondere. The same spond- root appears in sponsor, spouse, response and responsible, while English keeps the -ing ending fully productive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 spondere“许诺”，加前缀 com- 得到 correspondere。同一 spond- 词根出现在 sponsor、spouse、response、responsible 中，而英语的 -ing 词尾仍完全能产。

items.meaning: answering another item in form, function or place
items.meaningCN: 在形状、功能或位置上回应另一项（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: The corresponding figures are given in the appendix.
items.exampleCN: 相应数字见附录。

items.meaning: to match, agree, or exchange letters
items.meaningCN: 相符；对应；通信（com-“一起”+ respondere“回答”）
items.example: The results correspond closely with the earlier study.
items.exampleCN: 结果与早先的研究高度相符。

items.meaningCN: 往来书信；对应关系（-ence 状态名词）
items.example: The correspondence between the two sets is exact.
items.exampleCN: 两个集合之间的对应是精确的。

items.meaning: one who writes letters or reports
items.meaningCN: 通信者；记者（-ent 施事名词）
items.example: The correspondent interviewed three witnesses.
items.exampleCN: 这名记者采访了三位证人。

items.meaning: in a matching or proportional way
items.meaningCN: 相应地；成比例地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: Costs fell and, correspondingly, prices were cut.
items.exampleCN: 成本下降，价格也相应下调。

items.meaningCN: 回答；反应（re-“回”+ spondere“许诺”）
items.example: The system responds to sound within milliseconds.
items.exampleCN: 系统在几毫秒内对声音作出反应。

items.meaningCN: 回答；反应（respons- 词干 + 名词词尾）
items.example: There was no response to the second letter.
items.exampleCN: 第二封信没有得到回复。

items.meaningCN: 有责任的；可靠的（-ible“可……的”）
items.example: She is responsible for the laboratory records.
items.exampleCN: 她负责实验室的记录。

items.meaningCN: 赞助者；担保人（spons- + -or 施事）
items.example: A local firm sponsored the survey.
items.exampleCN: 一家本地公司赞助了这项调查。

definition_zh: 批判性地；关键地；危急地；严谨评判地
definition_en: in a way that judges and evaluates, or in a way that is decisive for an outcome or dangerously serious
core_image: 一把解剖刀在放大镜下切开薄薄一层纸
scene: The patient was critically ill when the ambulance arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 critically 是「危急地、病危地」（第 4 个义项：病情危及生命）；句意：救护车到达时，病人病情危急。图中可辨识物件：救护车、担架、心电监护仪、氧气面罩、急诊灯。

pos.zh: 批判性地；关键性地；危急地；以评判的方式

senses.title: Judging faults
senses.titleCN: 批判地：挑出问题地
senses.definition: in a way that points out faults or disapproves
senses.definitionCN: 以指出错误或不赞成的方式
senses.example: She spoke critically of the plan's cost.
senses.exampleCN: 她批评性地谈到了该计划的成本。
senses.why: Greek krinein means 'to separate and judge'. The -ly adverb names the manner of a judgment that separates good from bad and names the bad part aloud.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 krinein 意为“分开、判断”。-ly 副词指明的正是这样一种判断方式：把好坏分开，并把坏的部分说出来。

senses.title: Examining analytically
senses.titleCN: 分析性地：把文本拆开检验
senses.definition: in an analytical way that tests assumptions and evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以检验假设与证据的分析方式
senses.example: Students are taught to read critically rather than accept every claim.
senses.exampleCN: 学生被教导要批判性地阅读，而不是接受每一个说法。
senses.why: Criticism at its root is separation: the reader takes a claim apart into reasons and evidence, so the adverb describes analytical dismantling, not mere complaint.
senses.whyCN: 批判的词根义是“分开”：读者把主张拆成理由与证据，因此这个副词描写的是分析性的拆解，而非单纯抱怨。

senses.title: Decisively important
senses.titleCN: 关键地：决定成败地
senses.definition: in a way that is decisive for the success or failure of something
senses.definitionCN: 以决定某事成败的方式
senses.example: The next two weeks are critically important for the project.
senses.exampleCN: 接下来两周对项目至关重要。
senses.why: A 'critical' moment is a turning point where a judgment must be made. What happens there decides the outcome, so the adverb comes to mean 'decisively'.
senses.whyCN: critical 的时刻是必须作出判断的转折点，此时发生的事决定结局，于是副词引申为“决定性地、关键地”。

senses.title: Dangerously, near death
senses.titleCN: 危急地：病情危及生命
senses.definition: in a medically dangerous state that threatens life
senses.definitionCN: 处于危及生命的医疗危险状态
senses.example: Two passengers remained critically injured after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车后有两名乘客伤势危重。
senses.why: The medical sense comes from Greek krisis 'decision': a crisis is the point where the body either recovers or dies. 'Critically ill' means the patient is at exactly that point.
senses.whyCN: 医学义来自希腊语 krisis“决断”：危象是身体要么恢复、要么死亡的节点。critically ill 意为病人正处在那个节点上。

senses.title: At a threshold in physics
senses.titleCN: 临界地：正好落在阈值上
senses.definition: at the exact threshold where a system changes behaviour, as in a critically damped system
senses.definitionCN: 恰在系统改变行为的阈值上，如临界阻尼系统
senses.example: The needle returns to rest because the instrument is critically damped.
senses.exampleCN: 因为仪器处于临界阻尼状态，指针会回到静止位置。
senses.why: Physics takes 'critical' as the boundary between two regimes. Critically damped means the system sits exactly on that line, returning to rest as fast as possible without overshooting.
senses.whyCN: 物理把 critical 当作两种状态之间的界线。临界阻尼指系统恰好停在这条线上，以最快速度回到静止且不越过。

senses.title: Severely endangered
senses.titleCN: 极度地：濒危等级上的严重
senses.definition: in a severity category used for species close to extinction
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述接近灭绝物种的严重等级
senses.example: The frog is listed as critically endangered.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛙被列为极度濒危。
senses.why: Conservation ranks threat levels; 'critically' marks the highest step before extinction in the wild, extending the medical 'near the limit' sense to species.
senses.whyCN: 保护名录对威胁程度分级；critically 标记的是野外灭绝之前的最高一级，把医学“接近极限”的义项延伸到物种。

senses.title: By scholarly comparison of texts
senses.titleCN: 校勘地：依据版本比对定文本
senses.definition: as in a critical edition, where variant texts are compared to establish the best reading
senses.definitionCN: 如在校勘版中，通过比对不同文本确定最佳读法
senses.example: The play was critically edited from six early editions.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏剧依据六个早期版本进行了校勘编订。
senses.why: Textual criticism separates genuine readings from scribal errors. A critically edited text is one whose readings were judged and sorted by that method.
senses.whyCN: 文本校勘把真读与抄写错误分开。critically edited 的文本，就是其读法经过这种方法判断与归类后确定的文本。

senses.title: By professional evaluation
senses.titleCN: 评论界地：由专业评判给出
senses.definition: as judged by reviewers or professional critics
senses.definitionCN: 由评论人或专业批评家评判地
senses.example: The film was critically acclaimed but ignored by audiences.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片广受评论界好评，却不受观众关注。
senses.why: Critics are the people whose profession is judgment. 'Critically acclaimed' means the acclaim came from that judging group, whether or not the public agreed.
senses.whyCN: 评论家是以判断为职业的人。critically acclaimed 意为赞誉来自这一评判群体，不论公众是否认同。

intro.en: Critically is critic + -al + -ly, ultimately from Greek kritikos 'able to judge'. The stacking of two English suffixes on a Greek base is typical of modern academic vocabulary.
intro.cn: critically 由 critic + -al + -ly 构成，最终来自希腊语 kritikos“能作判断的”。在希腊词基上叠加两个英语后缀，是现代学术词汇的典型做法。

items.en: krinein meant 'to separate, sift, decide'. Judgment begins as separation: the judge sifts the evidence and sets one side apart from the other.
items.cn: krinein 意为“分开、筛选、决定”。判断始于分离：法官筛过证据，把一方与另一方分开。

items.en: kritikos 'able to judge or discern' and the noun kritēs 'judge' name the person and the capacity. The root also yields krisis 'a decision', the source of English crisis.
items.cn: kritikos“能判断、能辨识的”与名词 kritēs“法官”分别命名这种能力与执行者。同一词根还产生 krisis“决断”，即英语 crisis 的来源。

items.en: Latin criticus was borrowed from Greek and passed through French critique into English critic in the 16th century. The adjective critical followed in the 17th.
items.cn: 拉丁 criticus 借自希腊语，经法语 critique 于16世纪进入英语作 critic。形容词 critical 于17世纪随后出现。

items.en: Medical Latin used criticus for the 'decisive' day of a fever. From that came the modern sense 'dangerous, near a crisis', which explains critically ill.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 criticus 指发热的“决定日”。由此产生现代“危急、接近危象”的义项，这正是 critically ill 的由来。

items.en: critical is critic + -al 'relating to'; critically adds -ly, from Old English -lice, making an adverb of manner. The adverb can modify adjectives as well as verbs, as in critically important.
items.cn: critical 是 critic + -al“与……有关的”；critically 再加 -ly（来自古英语 -lice），构成方式副词。该副词既可修饰动词，也可修饰形容词，如 critically important。

items.en: Physics, conservation and textual scholarship each borrowed the adjective and fixed an adverb phrase: critically damped, critically endangered, critically edited. The dates of these technical uses are modern and approximate.
items.cn: 物理学、保护生物学与文本学各自借用了这个形容词并固定了副词短语：critically damped、critically endangered、critically edited。这些技术用法的年代属现代，具体为约数。

note.en: The first group differs chiefly in suffix or spelling; the second shares the 'serious / important' area but measures something else.
note.cn: 第一组主要在词尾或拼写上不同；第二组共享“严重／重要”语义区域，但衡量的是别的维度。

entries.definition: The adjective that critically derives from; it describes a thing or moment, not the manner of an action.
entries.definitionCN: critically 所由派生的形容词；它描述事物或时刻，而非动作的方式。

entries.definition: A person who judges works or expresses disapproval; it is a noun, not an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 评判作品或表达不满的人；是名词而非副词。

entries.definition: A detailed analysis and judgment, usually written; it stresses systematic assessment rather than manner.
entries.definitionCN: 通常为书面的详细分析与判断；强调系统评估，而非方式。

entries.definition: In a way that is decisively important; very close to sense 3, but it lacks the judging and medical branches.
entries.definitionCN: 以具有决定重要性的方式；与第 3 个义项很接近，但没有评判与医学分支。

entries.definition: To a very serious degree; it can replace critically in medical contexts but does not imply a threshold or crisis.
entries.definitionCN: 达到非常严重的程度；在医学语境可替换 critically，但不含阈值或危象之意。

entries.definition: By separating a whole into parts; close to sense 2, but without the evaluative edge of judging worth.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体拆成部分地；接近第 2 个义项，但没有评判价值的评价锋芒。

entries.definition: In a way that shows disapproval; it names the attitude, while critically names the method of judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 以显出不满的方式；它命名态度，而 critically 命名判断方法。

entries.definition: In a way that involves risk of harm; broader than sense 4, which is tied to a medical or ranked threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 以带有伤害风险的方式；比第 4 个义项更宽，后者与医学或分级阈值绑定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: genuine morphemes, standard collocations and the real critic word family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、标准搭配与真实的 critic 词族。

normal.en: krinein 'separate': a critic separates the good from the bad, and critically describes doing that in action.
normal.cn: krinein“分开”：评论家把好的与坏的分开，critically 描述的就是这种动作方式。

normal.en: critical + -ly: the adjective becomes an adverb of manner, and it can also modify adjectives, as in critically important.
normal.cn: critical + -ly：形容词变为方式副词，也可修饰形容词，如 critically important。

normal.en: Learn the fixed phrases critically ill, critically endangered, critically acclaimed and critically damped; each marks a different branch.
normal.cn: 记住固定短语 critically ill、critically endangered、critically acclaimed、critically damped；每个都标记不同分支。

normal.en: critic, critical, criticism, criticize and critique all descend from the same judging root.
normal.cn: critic、critical、criticism、criticize、critique 都出自同一个“判断”词根。

normal.en: crisis is a sibling: both come from krinein, and a crisis is literally the moment that demands a decision.
normal.cn: crisis 是同胞词：二者都来自 krinein，crisis 字面上就是“要求作出决断的时刻”。

abstract.en: Picture a scalpel cutting a sheet into two clean halves: that separation is the original judgment.
abstract.cn: 想象一把解剖刀把一张纸切成两半：这种分离就是最初的“判断”。

abstract.en: Picture a patient's monitor at the exact line between stable and failing: critically ill sits on that line.
abstract.cn: 想象病人的监护仪停在“稳定”与“衰竭”之间的那条线上：critically ill 就停在那条线上。

abstract.en: Picture a knife-edge balance that settles exactly level, neither tipping left nor right: critically damped.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃上的天平恰好水平停住，不向左也不向右倾：这就是 critically damped。

examples.en: The report examines critically the assumptions behind the model.
examples.cn: 报告批判性地检验了该模型背后的假设。

examples.en: Access to clean water is critically important in the first days after a disaster.
examples.cn: 灾后最初几天，获得清洁水至关重要。

examples.en: The species is now critically endangered across most of its range.
examples.cn: 该物种在其大部分分布区内现已极度濒危。

dict_mnemonic.text: “critic（评论家）+ ally（盟友）”——评论家带着刀一般的眼光站在你旁边 → critically 批判性地、关键地

root: 希腊 krinein“分开、判断”→ kritikos“能判断的”→ 拉丁 criticus → 英语 critic + -al + -ly；同根词还有 crisis、criterion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses branch from a judge's act of separating: separating faults, separating claims, separating the decisive moment, separating life from death, and separating true readings from errors.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从“判断者的分离动作”分叉：分出错误、拆开主张、分出决定性时刻、分出存亡、分出真读与讹误。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade separating one layer from another under a lens.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃在镜片下把一层与另一层分开。

branches.en: JUDGING TONE: finding fault and professional acclaim are the same judgment voiced negatively or positively.
branches.cn: 评判语气：挑错与专业赞誉，是同一判断的否定或肯定表达。

branches.en: ANALYTICAL SEPARATION: reading critically and editing a text critically both split a claim or a version into parts.
branches.cn: 分析性分离：批判性阅读与校勘编订，都把主张或版本拆成部分。

branches.en: THE DECISIVE POINT: a critical moment sits on the line that determines what follows.
branches.cn: 关键节点：决定性时刻恰在决定后续走向的那条线上。

branches.en: SEVERITY SCALE: critically ill and critically endangered place a life or a species at the highest danger rank.
branches.cn: 严重等级：critically ill 与 critically endangered 把生命或物种放到最高危险等级。

branches.en: PHYSICAL LIMIT: the physics sense makes the threshold literal, with a system changing regime at one exact point.
branches.cn: 物理极限：物理义把阈值字面化，系统在某个精确点上改变状态。

intro.en: Critically stacks -al and -ly on the borrowed base critic. Both suffixes are fully productive in English, while the Greek root kri- is no longer separable.
intro.cn: critically 在借入词基 critic 上叠加 -al 与 -ly。两个后缀在英语中都完全能产，而希腊词根 kri- 已不可再拆分。

latinIntro.en: Greek krinein 'to separate, decide' produced kritikos, krisis and kritērion, which Latin passed on as criticus and crisis. English then built critic, critical, criticism and criterion on these stems.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 krinein“分开、决定”产生 kritikos、krisis、kritērion，拉丁语将其传为 criticus 与 crisis。英语随后在这些词干上构造了 critic、critical、criticism、criterion。

items.meaning: in a judging or decisive manner
items.meaningCN: 以评判或决定性的方式（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The evidence was critically assessed by two reviewers.
items.exampleCN: 证据由两位评审进行了批判性评估。

items.meaning: judging, decisive, or at a crisis point
items.meaningCN: 批判的；关键的；危急的（-al“与……有关”）
items.example: The next step is critical to the whole design.
items.exampleCN: 下一步对整个设计至关重要。

items.meaning: one who judges works or conduct
items.meaningCN: 评论家；批评者（经拉丁 criticus 来自希腊 kritēs“法官”）
items.example: The critic praised the novel's structure.
items.exampleCN: 评论家称赞了这部小说的结构。

items.meaningCN: 批评的实践；指责（-ism 构成体系或行为名词）
items.example: Literary criticism took shape as a university subject.
items.exampleCN: 文学批评作为大学学科成形。

items.meaningCN: 批评；指责；分析（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The paper was criticized for its small sample.
items.exampleCN: 该论文因样本量小受到批评。

items.meaningCN: 系统的书面评论（经法语 critique，源自希腊 kritikē）
items.example: She wrote a critique of the exhibition.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一篇关于该展览的评论。

items.meaningCN: 判断标准（希腊 kritērion“判断工具”）
items.example: Cost is only one criterion for choosing a site.
items.exampleCN: 成本只是选址的标准之一。

items.meaningCN: 危急关头；决定性转折（经拉丁来自希腊 krisis“决断”）
items.example: The drought became a food crisis.
items.exampleCN: 干旱演变成粮食危机。

items.meaning: pretending to hold beliefs one does not hold
items.meaningCN: 伪善（希腊 hypo-“在下”+ krinein“判断／演戏”）
items.example: The scandal exposed the hypocrisy of the campaign.
items.exampleCN: 丑闻暴露了这场运动的伪善。

items.meaningCN: 内分泌的（endo-“在内”+ krinein“分开”）
items.example: The endocrine system regulates growth.
items.exampleCN: 内分泌系统调节生长。

latinEntries.meaning: a means or standard of judging

definition_zh: 批评；指责；评论；批判性研究
definition_en: the act of pointing out faults, or the systematic analysis and judgment of a work or idea
core_image: 一根手指点向画布上的裂痕，旁边摊着写满批注的稿纸
scene: The plan drew sharp criticism from local residents.
sceneCN: 这里 criticism 是「批评、指责」（第 1 个义项：对某事表示不满）；句意：这项计划遭到当地居民的严厉批评。图中可辨识物件：规划图、批注稿纸、指向前方的手、居民代表、麦克风。

pos.zh: 批评；指责（不可数）；一条批评意见（可数）；评论；批判性研究

derivatives.zh: 批判性地；关键地；危急地

senses.title: Fault-finding
senses.titleCN: 批评指责：指出做得不好的地方
senses.definition: the act of saying that something is wrong or unsatisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 指出某事有误或不能令人满意的行为
senses.example: The decision to close the library met with widespread criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 关闭图书馆的决定遭到广泛批评。
senses.why: criticism begins as judgment by separation: the critic separates the faulty part from the rest and names it. The disapproving sense is the everyday form of that separation.
senses.whyCN: criticism 始于“分离式判断”：批评者把有问题的部分与其余部分分开并指出。指责义就是这种分离的日常形态。

senses.title: A specific objection
senses.titleCN: 一条具体批评：可数的那句指责
senses.definition: a particular statement pointing out a fault
senses.definitionCN: 指出某一缺点的具体说法
senses.example: The report lists three criticisms of the current procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了对现行程序的三条批评。
senses.why: The countable plural turns the general attitude into discrete items: each objection is one separated fault, counted and listed.
senses.whyCN: 可数复数把总体态度变成一条条项目：每条反对意见都是一个被分离出来的缺点，可以计数、可以列举。

senses.title: Judging a work's merits
senses.titleCN: 作品评论：既看优点也看缺点
senses.definition: the analysis and evaluation of a work of art, literature or thought
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术、文学或思想作品的分析与评价
senses.example: Her criticism of the novel balances praise with close reading.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这部小说的评论把赞誉与细读结合起来。
senses.why: In this sense the separation is not hostile: the critic separates strengths from weaknesses and weighs both, so criticism can be positive.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，分离并不带敌意：评论者把优点与缺点分开并权衡两者，因此 criticism 也可以是正面评价。

senses.title: A critical essay
senses.titleCN: 评论文章：成篇的评判
senses.definition: a written piece that analyses and judges a work
senses.definitionCN: 分析并评判某作品的书面文章
senses.example: He published a criticism of the exhibition in a weekly magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一本周刊上发表了一篇关于该展览的评论文章。
senses.why: The abstract practice becomes a countable product: one essay is one occasion of judging, printed and dated.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的实践变成可数的产物：一篇文章就是一次判断的产物，有发表处、有日期。

senses.title: The academic discipline
senses.titleCN: 批评学科：文学批评这一门学问
senses.definition: the scholarly field that studies how works are interpreted and evaluated
senses.definitionCN: 研究作品如何被解释与评价的学术领域
senses.example: Modern criticism asks how readers' assumptions shape interpretation.
senses.exampleCN: 现代批评研究读者的预设如何塑造解释。
senses.why: A method of judgment can itself become an object of study. The discipline studies the act of separating and judging, not just particular works.
senses.whyCN: 判断方法本身也可以成为研究对象。这门学科研究“分离与判断”这一行为，而不只是具体作品。

senses.title: Textual criticism
senses.titleCN: 校勘学：比对版本，判断真读
senses.definition: the scholarly comparison of manuscript or printed versions to establish an accurate text
senses.definitionCN: 比对手稿或印刷版本以确定准确文本的学术工作
senses.example: Textual criticism showed that two lines had been added by a later editor.
senses.exampleCN: 校勘表明有两行是后来的编者添加的。
senses.why: Here the critic literally separates readings: genuine words are sorted from copying errors and later insertions, and the text is rebuilt from what survives that test.
senses.whyCN: 这里的批评者是字面意义上的“分离者”：真读被从抄误与后加内容中挑出，文本据通过检验的部分重建。

senses.title: Self-criticism
senses.titleCN: 自我批评：把刀口对准自己
senses.definition: the examination and condemnation of one's own conduct or beliefs
senses.definitionCN: 对自己行为或信念的检查与谴责
senses.example: The group ended every meeting with a round of self-criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小组每次会议都以一轮自我批评结束。
senses.why: The judging separation is turned inward: the person splits their own conduct into acceptable and faulty parts, and speaks the faulty part aloud.
senses.whyCN: 判断性的分离转向自身：人把自己的行为分成可接受与有错的部分，并把有错的部分说出来。

senses.title: Critique of an idea or system
senses.titleCN: 思想批判：检验一套观念的前提
senses.definition: a systematic philosophical examination of the limits or assumptions of an idea, system or institution
senses.definitionCN: 对某一观念、体系或制度的前提与界限所作的系统哲学检验
senses.example: Kant's criticism of pure reason examined what the mind can and cannot know.
senses.exampleCN: 康德对纯粹理性的批判考察了心灵能知道什么、不能知道什么。
senses.why: Philosophical criticism does not merely find faults; it separates the conditions under which a claim is valid from those under which it collapses.
senses.whyCN: 哲学批判并不只是挑错；它把一个主张成立的条件与失效的条件分开。

intro.en: Criticism is critic + -ism, from Greek kritikē technē 'the judging art'. The word first named fault-finding and only later became the name of a scholarly discipline.
intro.cn: criticism 由 critic + -ism 构成，源自希腊 kritikē technē“判断的技艺”。这个词最初指挑错，后来才成为一门学科的名称。

items.en: krinein 'to separate, decide' gave kritikos 'able to judge' and the art called kritikē. The original activity is discrimination, not hostility.
items.cn: krinein“分开、决定”产生 kritikos“能判断的”，以及被称为 kritikē 的技艺。其原始活动是辨别，而非敌意。

items.en: Latin criticus and French critique carried the word westward. English critic appears in the 16th century, naming a person who judges texts or conduct.
items.cn: 拉丁 criticus 与法语 critique 把这个词西传。英语 critic 于16世纪出现，指判断文本或行为的人。

items.en: criticism enters English in the early 17th century with the sense 'the act of censuring or finding fault'. The hostile sense is therefore old, but it is not the root meaning.
items.cn: criticism 于17世纪初进入英语，意为“谴责、挑错的行为”。敌意义因此很古老，但并非词根本义。

items.en: By the late 17th and 18th centuries criticism had become the name for the reasoned evaluation of literature and art, producing the modern phrase literary criticism.
items.cn: 到17世纪末与18世纪，criticism 已成为对文学与艺术进行理性评价的名称，并产生现代短语 literary criticism。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries the word widened into a university field, and 'theory' was added to name the study of interpretation itself. Dates are approximate.
items.cn: 19、20世纪，这个词扩展为一门大学学科，并加上“理论”来命名对解释本身的研究。年代为约数。

items.en: The exact first recorded date of criticism and the precise split between 'censure' and 'evaluation' are uncertain. The deeper origin of krinein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: criticism 最早的确切记录年代，以及“谴责”与“评价”之间的精确分化时间，均存疑。krinein 的更深来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains closely spelled relatives with different jobs; the second contains words for negative judgment or for evaluation.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近、功能不同的同族词；第二组是表示否定判断或评价的词。

entries.definition: The person who judges or finds fault; criticism is the activity or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 作出判断或挑错的人；criticism 是这一活动或其产物。

entries.definition: A detailed written analysis, often more neutral and academic than criticism in its fault-finding sense.
entries.definitionCN: 详细的书面分析，通常比“挑错”义的 criticism 更中性、更学术。

entries.definition: The state of being critical, especially in nuclear engineering; it is not the activity of judging.
entries.definitionCN: 处于临界的状态，尤其用于核工程；不是评判活动。

entries.definition: Official or formal condemnation; stronger and more institutional than everyday criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 官方或正式的谴责；比日常 criticism 更强、更具制度性。

entries.definition: An assessment of a work published in a newspaper or journal; it is usually a single piece, not the whole practice.
entries.definitionCN: 在报刊上发表的评介；通常是一篇文章，而非整个实践。

entries.definition: A judgment based on criteria; it is neutral and systematic, without the fault-finding edge.
entries.definitionCN: 依据标准作出的判断；中性且系统，没有挑错的锋芒。

entries.definition: An unfavourable opinion; it names the attitude, while criticism can also be a reasoned analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 不赞成的看法；它命名态度，而 criticism 也可以是理性分析。

entries.definition: The separation of a whole into parts; it lacks the explicit judgment that criticism carries.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体拆成部分；不含 criticism 所带的明确评判。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and the genuine critic family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实的 critic 词族。

normal.en: critic + -ism: -ism turns the person's activity into a named practice or system.
normal.cn: critic + -ism：-ism 把个人的活动变成一种被命名的实践或体系。

normal.en: Criticism is uncountable when it means the activity, countable when it means individual objections.
normal.cn: criticism 指活动时不可数，指一条条具体意见时可数。

normal.en: Learn literary criticism, textual criticism and self-criticism; these three phrases mark the main branches.
normal.cn: 记住 literary criticism、textual criticism、self-criticism；这三个短语标记了主要分支。

normal.en: critic, criticism, criticize, critical and critique all keep the kri- judging core.
normal.cn: critic、criticism、criticize、critical、critique 都保留 kri- 的判断核心。

normal.en: Constructive criticism is the positive collocation: the separation is meant to improve, not merely to wound.
normal.cn: constructive criticism 是正面搭配：这种分离意在改进，而不只是伤人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a crack in a painting while a notebook records each flaw.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿画作上的裂痕移动，同时有一本笔记记录每处缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture two piles on a desk, one labelled 'keep' and one labelled 'fix'; criticism is the sorting.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两堆纸，一堆写“保留”，一堆写“要改”；criticism 就是这次分拣。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror turned inward, where the person judges their own reflection by the same blade.
abstract.cn: 想象一面转向内部的镜子，人用同一把刀评判镜中的自己。

examples.en: The proposal came under criticism for ignoring the needs of smaller towns.
examples.cn: 该提案因忽视小城镇的需求而受到批评。

examples.en: Her book offers a balanced criticism of the government's housing policy.
examples.cn: 她的书对政府的住房政策作了平衡的评论。

examples.en: Biblical criticism compares manuscripts to recover the earliest text.
examples.cn: 圣经校勘学通过比对抄本来复原最早的文本。

dict_mnemonic.text: “critic（评论家）+ ism（主义）”——评论家把挑错变成一门主义 → criticism 批评、评论

root: 希腊 krinein“分开、判断”→ kritikē“判断的技艺”→ 拉丁 criticus → 英语 critic + -ism 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share the act of separating: faults from merits, one objection from another, true readings from errors, and one's own conduct into acceptable and faulty parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享“分离”动作：把缺点与优点分开、把一条意见与另一条分开、把真读与讹误分开，以及把自己的行为分成可接受与有错的部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing at one flaw while a notebook lists the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指点向一处缺陷，笔记本把其余问题逐条列下。

branches.en: DISAPPROVAL: the general attitude and the single countable objection are the same fault named at two scales.
branches.cn: 不赞成：总体态度与单条可数意见，是同一缺点在两种尺度上的命名。

branches.en: EVALUATION: judging a work’s merits, seeing both strengths and weaknesses.
branches.cn: 评价：评判作品优劣，既看优点也看缺点。

branches.en: METHOD: the academic discipline and textual criticism both study or apply the rules of separating true from false.
branches.cn: 方法：学科与校勘学都在研究或应用“分出真伪”的规则。

branches.en: INWARD AND PHILOSOPHICAL: self-criticism turns the blade inward; philosophical criticism separates the conditions under which a claim holds.
branches.cn: 向内与哲学化：自我批评把刀口转向自身；哲学批判则分开主张成立与失效的条件。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN PRODUCT: a criticism in a magazine is one printed act of judging, with a date and a byline.
branches.cn: 书面产物：杂志上的一篇 criticism 是一次被印出来的判断，有日期、有署名。

intro.en: Criticism is critic + -ism, a productive English suffix for practices, systems and doctrines. The base critic comes from Greek through Latin and French.
intro.cn: criticism 由 critic + -ism 构成，-ism 是能产的英语后缀，表示实践、体系或主义。词基 critic 经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语。

latinIntro.en: Greek krinein 'to separate, judge' supplies kritikos, krisis and kritērion; Latin criticus and French critique carry the stems into English critic, criticism, critical and criterion.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 krinein“分开、判断”提供 kritikos、krisis、kritērion；拉丁 criticus 与法语 critique 把这些词干带入英语 critic、criticism、critical、criterion。

items.meaning: the practice of judging; a written evaluation
items.meaningCN: 评判的实践；书面评论（-ism 表示实践或体系）
items.example: The article offers a fair criticism of the new policy.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章对新政策作了公正的批评。

items.meaning: a person who judges works or conduct
items.meaningCN: 评论家；批评者（经拉丁 criticus 来自希腊 kritēs“法官”）
items.example: The critic found the production uneven.
items.exampleCN: 评论家认为这部制作水准参差。

items.meaningCN: 批判的；关键的；危急的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: The review was critical but fair.
items.exampleCN: 这篇评论尖锐但公正。

items.meaning: in a judging or decisive way
items.meaningCN: 以批判或决定性的方式（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The claim was critically tested by the team.
items.exampleCN: 该说法由团队进行了批判性检验。

items.meaning: to find fault with; to analyse
items.meaningCN: 批评；指责；分析（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The auditor criticized the lack of records.
items.exampleCN: 审计员批评了记录缺失的问题。

items.meaningCN: 系统的书面评论（法语 critique，源自希腊 kritikē）
items.example: The seminar produced a detailed critique of the draft.
items.exampleCN: 研讨班对草稿提出了详细评论。

items.meaningCN: 判断用的标准（希腊 kritērion）
items.example: The main criterion was durability, not price.
items.exampleCN: 主要标准是耐用性，而非价格。

items.meaningCN: 决定性转折；危机（经拉丁来自希腊 krisis）
items.example: The shortage turned into a political crisis.
items.exampleCN: 短缺演变为政治危机。

items.meaningCN: 吹毛求疵的（hyper-“过度”+ critical）
items.example: He was hypercritical of every draft.
items.exampleCN: 他对每份草稿都吹毛求疵。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 判断的技艺（希腊 kritikē technē）

definition_zh: 关键的；批判的；危急的；临界的
definition_en: decisively important, judging or analytical, or at a dangerous turning point
core_image: 秒表的指针停在红色刻线上，旁边的烧杯正要倾倒
scene: Timing is critical when the two chemicals are mixed.
sceneCN: 这里 critical 是「关键的」（第 1 个义项：决定结果的关键时刻）；句意：混合这两种化学品时，时机至关重要。图中可辨识物件：秒表、烧杯、滴管、红色警示灯、实验台。

pos.zh: 关键的；批判的；危急的；临界的；校勘的

derivatives.zh: 批判性地；关键地；危急地

senses.title: Decisively important
senses.titleCN: 关键的：决定成败的
senses.definition: so important that it decides the success or failure of something
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以决定某事成败的
senses.example: The first ten minutes are critical in this experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个实验里，最初十分钟至关重要。
senses.why: A critical moment is the point where a decision is made and the outcome turns. The adjective moves from 'of a crisis' to 'decisive' because both name a point that settles what follows.
senses.whyCN: critical 的时刻是作出决定、结局转向的节点。形容词从“危象的”转为“决定性的”，因为两者都指决定后续走向的节点。

senses.title: Finding fault
senses.titleCN: 批评的：指出缺点的
senses.definition: expressing disapproval or pointing out faults
senses.definitionCN: 表达不赞成或指出缺点的
senses.example: The report was critical of the department's record-keeping.
senses.exampleCN: 报告对部门的记录工作持批评态度。
senses.why: The judging root krinein separates good from bad. A critical remark does the separating in public, naming the part that fails.
senses.whyCN: 判断词根 krinein 把好与坏分开。critical 的言论就是把这种分离公开做出来，指出不合格的部分。

senses.title: Analytical thinking
senses.titleCN: 批判性思维的：拆开检验的
senses.definition: involving careful analysis of claims and evidence rather than passive acceptance
senses.definitionCN: 对主张与证据进行仔细分析、而非被动接受的
senses.example: Critical thinking requires students to question the source of every statistic.
senses.exampleCN: 批判性思维要求学生质疑每项统计数据的来源。
senses.why: Here judgment is applied to reasoning itself: the thinker separates premises from conclusions and tests the link, so the adjective names a method rather than an attitude.
senses.whyCN: 这里的判断作用于推理本身：思考者把前提与结论分开并检验其联系，因此形容词命名的是一种方法，而非态度。

senses.title: Medically dangerous
senses.titleCN: 危重的：病情可能致命的
senses.definition: in a medical state in which death or serious harm is possible
senses.definitionCN: 处于可能死亡或受到严重伤害的医疗状态
senses.example: He was listed as critical after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后他被列为危重病人。
senses.why: Medical Latin used criticus for the decisive day of a fever. A critical patient is at that decisive point, where the body may recover or fail.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语用 criticus 指发热的决定日。危重病人正处在这个决定点上，身体可能恢复，也可能衰竭。

senses.title: At a physics threshold
senses.titleCN: 临界的：跨过就会变状态的
senses.definition: at the exact value at which a physical system changes behaviour, as in critical mass or critical temperature
senses.definitionCN: 物理系统改变行为的精确数值点，如临界质量或临界温度
senses.example: Below critical mass, the chain reaction cannot sustain itself.
senses.exampleCN: 低于临界质量时，链式反应无法自我维持。
senses.why: Physics makes the 'decisive point' literal: on one side of the value the system behaves one way, on the other side another way. The adjective names the boundary itself.
senses.whyCN: 物理把“决定点”字面化：数值一侧系统如此行为，另一侧则另一种行为。形容词命名的正是这条边界。

senses.title: Of textual scholarship
senses.titleCN: 校勘的：依据版本判断真读的
senses.definition: relating to the scholarly comparison of texts to establish an accurate version
senses.definitionCN: 与通过比对文本确定准确版本有关的
senses.example: The critical edition records every variant in a footnote.
senses.exampleCN: 校勘版在脚注中记录每一处异文。
senses.why: A critical edition is one in which the editor has separated authentic readings from errors and defended the choice. The adjective marks the judgment behind the text.
senses.whyCN: 校勘版是编者把真读与讹误分开并论证取舍的版本。这个形容词标记的正是文本背后的判断。

senses.title: Essential infrastructure
senses.titleCN: 关键基础设施的：社会离不开的
senses.definition: designating systems whose failure would seriously disrupt society, as in critical national infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 指失效会严重扰乱社会的系统，如国家关键基础设施
senses.example: Power grids and water plants are classified as critical infrastructure.
senses.exampleCN: 电网与水厂被归类为关键基础设施。
senses.why: Security policy extends 'decisive' from a moment to a system: if this fails, everything that depends on it fails, so it stands at the decisive point of the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 安全政策把“决定性的”从时刻延伸到系统：若它失效，依赖它的一切都会失效，因此它位于整个网络的决定点上。

senses.title: A written evaluative review
senses.titleCN: 评论性的：成篇评判的
senses.definition: of a written piece that analyses and judges a work, as in a critical review
senses.definitionCN: 指分析并评判某作品的书面文章，如评论性综述
senses.example: She wrote a critical review of the new translation.
senses.exampleCN: 她为新译本写了一篇评论性书评。
senses.why: The written product keeps the balanced sense of criticism: it separates strengths from weaknesses and states a verdict, which is why 'critical review' need not mean a hostile one.
senses.whyCN: 书面产物保留了 criticism 的平衡义：它把优点与缺点分开并给出结论，因此 critical review 未必是敌意的。

intro.en: Critical is critic + -al, from Greek kritikos through Latin criticus. Its medical sense came first in English; the 'important' sense is a later extension.
intro.cn: critical 由 critic + -al 构成，经拉丁 criticus 来自希腊 kritikos。在英语中医学义先出现，“重要”义是后来的延伸。

items.en: krinein 'to separate, decide' produced kritikos 'able to judge' and krisis 'decision'. The family is about sorting and deciding, not about complaining.
items.cn: krinein“分开、决定”产生 kritikos“能判断的”与 krisis“决断”。这个词族关乎分拣与决定，而非抱怨。

items.en: Latin criticus was used for the 'decisive' day of a disease, when the patient's fate became clear. This medical sense travelled into early English.
items.cn: 拉丁 criticus 用于疾病的“决定日”，即病人命运变得清楚的时刻。这个医学义进入早期英语。

items.en: English critic named a judge of literature; critical followed in the 17th century, first meaning 'relating to judgment or to a crisis'.
items.cn: 英语 critic 指文学评判者；critical 于17世纪随后出现，最初意为“与判断或危象有关的”。

items.en: From the idea of a decisive turning point, critical widened in the 18th and 19th centuries to mean 'vitally important' in general, a sense that now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 从“决定性转折点”的观念出发，critical 在18、19世纪扩展为泛指“极其重要”，这一义项如今主导日常用法。

items.en: Physics and engineering adopted critical for a threshold value in the 19th century; critical mass became prominent with nuclear physics in the 20th. Dates are approximate.
items.cn: 物理与工程在19世纪采用 critical 表示阈值；critical mass 随20世纪核物理而显著流行。年代为约数。

items.en: The exact date at which 'important' overtook 'crisis' in frequency is not recorded with certainty. The deeper etymology of krinein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: “重要”义在频率上超过“危象”义的确切年代没有可靠记录。krinein 的更深词源属重构。

note.en: The first group differs in suffix or part of speech; the second contains words that cover one branch of critical but not the others.
note.cn: 第一组在词尾或词性上不同；第二组各覆盖 critical 的一个分支，但不同时覆盖其他分支。

entries.definition: The adverb of manner; it modifies verbs or adjectives, while critical modifies nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 方式副词，修饰动词或形容词；而 critical 修饰名词。

entries.definition: The activity or product of judging; it is not a synonym for the adjective critical.
entries.definitionCN: 评判的活动或产物；不是形容词 critical 的同义词。

entries.definition: A person who judges; the adjective critical can describe that person's remarks but not replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作出评判的人；形容词 critical 可描述其言论，但不能替代这个名词。

entries.definition: Decisively important for an outcome; it covers sense 1 but has no judging, medical or physics branches.
entries.definitionCN: 对结果具有决定重要性；覆盖第 1 个义项，但没有评判、医学或物理分支。

entries.definition: Showing an unfavourable opinion; it matches sense 2 but cannot mean 'important'.
entries.definitionCN: 显出不利看法；对应第 2 个义项，但不能表示“重要”。

entries.definition: Using separation into parts; close to sense 3, but without the element of judgment or evaluation.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体拆成部分；接近第 3 个义项，但不含判断或评价成分。

entries.definition: In medicine, severe and sudden; it overlaps sense 4 but does not imply a life-or-death turning point.
entries.definitionCN: 医学上指严重而突发；与第 4 个义项重叠，但不含生死转折点之意。

entries.definition: Absolutely necessary; close to sense 1, but it states need rather than a decisive moment.
entries.definitionCN: 绝对必要；接近第 1 个义项，但说的是“必需”，而非决定性时刻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, fixed collocations and the genuine critic family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、固定搭配与真实的 critic 词族。

normal.en: krinein 'separate, decide': a critical point is where the decision is made and the outcome separates into success or failure.
normal.cn: krinein“分开、决定”：critical 的点就是作出决定、结局分成成败两边的位置。

normal.en: critical + -al: the adjective can describe a moment, a person's attitude, a threshold or an edition.
normal.cn: critical + -al：这个形容词可描述时刻、态度、阈值或版本。

normal.en: Learn critical of, critical to, critical thinking, critical condition and critical mass; each phrase opens a different sense.
normal.cn: 记住 critical of、critical to、critical thinking、critical condition、critical mass；每个短语通向不同义项。

normal.en: critic, criticism, criticize, critically and criterion are all siblings from the same judging root.
normal.cn: critic、criticism、criticize、critically、criterion 都是同一判断词根的同胞词。

normal.en: Note the preposition change: critical of means disapproving, critical to means essential.
normal.cn: 注意介词差别：critical of 表示不满，critical to 表示必不可少。

abstract.en: Picture a stopwatch hand resting on a red line: one second earlier or later changes everything.
abstract.cn: 想象秒表指针停在红线上：早一秒或晚一秒，一切都会不同。

abstract.en: Picture a reactor's gauge crossing a marked value, after which the reaction sustains itself.
abstract.cn: 想象反应堆仪表越过一个标记值，此后反应便能自我维持。

abstract.en: Picture an editor with two manuscripts, choosing one reading and crossing out the other.
abstract.cn: 想象编者拿着两份抄本，选定一种读法，划掉另一种。

examples.en: Accurate measurements are critical to the reliability of the results.
examples.cn: 精确测量对结果的可靠性至关重要。

examples.en: The editorial was critical of the government's handling of the drought.
examples.cn: 社论对政府应对干旱的方式持批评态度。

examples.en: The patient remained in critical condition overnight.
examples.cn: 病人整夜处于危重状态。

dict_mnemonic.text: “critic（评论家）+ al（全部）”——评论家把全部问题都挑出来，也在最要紧处叫停 → critical 批判的、关键的、危急的

root: 希腊 krinein“分开、判断”→ kritikos“能判断的”→ 拉丁 criticus（含“决定日”医学义）→ 英语 critic + -al 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one idea: a point where a judgment separates outcomes. The judgment may be about faults, about evidence, about a patient, about a reactor, or about a manuscript.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个观念：判断把结局分开的那个点。判断可以针对缺点、证据、病人、反应堆或抄本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting on a red line that divides two outcomes.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在划分两种结局的红线上。

branches.en: DECISIVE IMPORTANCE: a critical moment and critical infrastructure both sit where failure would change everything.
branches.cn: 决定重要性：关键时刻与关键基础设施，都位于失效就会改变一切的位置。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: fault-finding names the bad part.
branches.cn: 判断：挑错指出坏的部分。

branches.en: DANGER AND THRESHOLD: a critical patient is at the point of survival or death; a critical mass is the point where a reaction sustains itself.
branches.cn: 危险与阈值：危重病人处于生与死的点上；临界质量是反应得以自持的点。

branches.en: SCHOLARLY JUDGMENT: a critical edition and a critical review both separate good readings or strengths from what fails.
branches.cn: 学术判断：校勘版与评论性文章，都把好的读法或优点与不合格者分开。

branches.en: METHOD: critical thinking is the adjective turned into a teachable skill of analysis.
branches.cn: 方法：critical thinking 把这个形容词变成一种可教授的分析技能。

intro.en: Critical is critic + -al, with the Latin stem critic- and a productive English adjective suffix. The prefix-like elements of the original Greek verb are no longer separable.
intro.cn: critical 由 critic + -al 构成，词干 critic- 来自拉丁语，-al 是能产的英语形容词后缀。原希腊动词的前缀成分已不可再分。

latinIntro.en: Greek krinein 'to separate, decide' yields kritikos, krisis and kritērion; Latin criticus carries the judging sense into English critic, critical, criticism and criterion.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 krinein“分开、决定”产生 kritikos、krisis、kritērion；拉丁 criticus 把判断义带入英语 critic、critical、criticism、criterion。

items.meaningCN: 批判的；关键的；临界的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: The choice of sample size is critical.
items.exampleCN: 样本量的选择至关重要。

items.meaning: one who judges works or conduct
items.meaningCN: 评论家；批评者（经拉丁 criticus 来自希腊 kritēs）
items.example: The critic reviewed three new novels.
items.exampleCN: 这位评论家评论了三部新小说。

items.meaning: the activity of judging; a written evaluation
items.meaningCN: 评判活动；书面评论（-ism 表实践）
items.example: The policy drew criticism from both sides.
items.exampleCN: 该政策受到双方批评。

items.meaningCN: 以批判或危急的方式（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The material is critically dependent on temperature.
items.exampleCN: 该材料关键性地依赖温度。

items.meaningCN: 批评；指责（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Reviewers criticized the paper's method.
items.exampleCN: 评审批评了论文的方法。

items.meaningCN: 系统评论（法语 critique，源自希腊 kritikē）
items.example: The book is a critique of modern economics.
items.exampleCN: 这本书是对现代经济学的批判。

items.meaningCN: 判断标准（希腊 kritērion）
items.example: Safety was the first criterion.
items.exampleCN: 安全是第一标准。

items.meaningCN: 决定性转折；危机
items.example: The bank survived the financial crisis.
items.exampleCN: 银行挺过了金融危机。

items.meaning: the state of being critical, especially in a reactor
items.meaningCN: 临界状态；关键性（-ity 状态名词）
items.example: Operators monitor the reactor's criticality.
items.exampleCN: 操作员监测反应堆的临界状态。

definition_zh: 标准；准则；尺度；判断依据
definition_en: a standard or principle by which something is judged, measured or selected
core_image: 一把带刻度的尺子横放在两张待选的纸上
scene: Cost was the main criterion for choosing the new site.
sceneCN: 这里 criterion 是「标准、准则」（第 2 个义项：选择所依据的条件）；句意：成本是选择新址的主要标准。图中可辨识物件：刻度尺、两张地图、厂房草图、价格标签、比对表。

pos.zh: 标准；准则；尺度（复数 criteria；criterions 极为罕见）

forms.label: 复数（希腊语 -on → -a）
forms.form: criteria（两个及以上标准；不可写作 criterias）

forms.label: 罕见复数
forms.form: criterions（少数旧用法，规范写作中应避免）

derivatives.zh: 标准参照的（教育测评术语）

senses.title: A standard for judging
senses.titleCN: 判断标准：拿来衡量对错的尺子
senses.definition: a principle or standard used to form a judgment
senses.definitionCN: 用于形成判断的原则或标准
senses.example: Fairness should be the criterion for judging the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 公平应是评判这项政策的标准。
senses.why: Greek kritērion is literally a 'means of judging', from kritēs 'judge'. The word names the tool the judge holds, not the judgment itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 kritērion 字面就是“判断的工具”，来自 kritēs“法官”。这个词命名的是法官手中的工具，而非判断本身。

senses.title: A requirement for selection
senses.titleCN: 选择条件：入选必须满足的那一条
senses.definition: a condition that a person, product or proposal must meet to be chosen
senses.definitionCN: 个人、产品或提案被选中必须满足的条件
senses.example: Cost was the main criterion for choosing the new site.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是选择新址的主要标准。
senses.why: Selection is judgment applied to options: the criterion is the measured line a candidate must reach to be kept rather than dropped.
senses.whyCN: 选择就是作用于选项的判断：标准是候选人必须达到的刻度，未达到就被淘汰。

senses.title: A measure in research
senses.titleCN: 研究指标：纳入与排除的依据
senses.definition: a defined measure used to include, exclude or classify cases in a study
senses.definitionCN: 研究中用于纳入、排除或分类病例的明确指标
senses.example: Age was an exclusion criterion in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 年龄是该试验的一项排除标准。
senses.why: Research must make judgment repeatable, so it converts a broad standard into an explicit measure that every researcher can apply identically.
senses.whyCN: 研究必须让判断可重复，因此把宽泛标准转化为每位研究者都能同样执行的明确指标。

senses.title: A legal test
senses.titleCN: 法律检验标准：法院据此判断
senses.definition: the test a court applies to decide a legal question
senses.definitionCN: 法院用来裁断法律问题的检验标准
senses.example: The court applied a three-part criterion for liability.
senses.exampleCN: 法院对责任适用了三部分检验标准。
senses.why: Law needs a public, stable measure so that similar cases receive similar rulings; the criterion is the visible line the court draws.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要公开、稳定的尺度，使相似案件得到相似裁决；标准就是法院画出的那条可见界线。

senses.title: A diagnostic criterion
senses.titleCN: 诊断标准：医生据此判定疾病
senses.definition: a specified feature or set of features used to identify a disease
senses.definitionCN: 用于识别某种疾病的特定特征或特征组合
senses.example: Persistent fatigue is one diagnostic criterion for the syndrome.
senses.exampleCN: 持续疲劳是该综合征的一项诊断标准。
senses.why: Medicine turns clinical judgment into shared criteria so that two doctors looking at the same patient reach the same diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 医学把临床判断变成共享标准，使两位医生面对同一位病人时得出相同诊断。

senses.title: An engineering specification
senses.titleCN: 工程设计准则：必须达到的参数
senses.definition: a required performance or design value that a product must satisfy
senses.definitionCN: 产品必须满足的性能或设计数值要求
senses.example: Load-bearing capacity was the key design criterion.
senses.exampleCN: 承重能力是关键的设计准则。
senses.why: Engineering converts a general aim such as safety into numbers that can be tested; the criterion is that aim made measurable.
senses.whyCN: 工程把安全之类的总体目标转化为可检验的数值；标准就是被量化后的目标。

senses.title: A test of truth
senses.titleCN: 真理标准：判断真假的依据
senses.definition: in philosophy, a principle used to distinguish true statements from false ones
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中用于区分真陈述与假陈述的原则
senses.example: Philosophers have proposed coherence as a criterion of truth.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家提出融贯性作为真理标准。
senses.why: Epistemology asks what tool justifies calling a belief true; the criterion is the rule that decides which claims pass the test.
senses.whyCN: 认识论追问用什么工具才能证明一个信念为真；标准就是决定哪些主张通过检验的规则。

senses.title: A scoring criterion
senses.titleCN: 评分标准：打分表上的每一条
senses.definition: a stated item in a rubric used to award marks or grades
senses.definitionCN: 评分量规中用于给分的明确条目
senses.example: Clarity of argument is the first scoring criterion.
senses.exampleCN: 论证清晰度是第一项评分标准。
senses.why: Education makes grading accountable by publishing the criteria in advance, so that the student can see the line the marker will use.
senses.whyCN: 教育通过事先公布标准使评分可问责，让学生看见评卷者将使用的刻度。

intro.en: Criterion is a Greek loanword built on the judge's root. Its Greek plural criteria is still the standard English plural, which is why 'criterias' is wrong.
intro.cn: criterion 是建立在“法官”词根上的希腊借词。其希腊复数 criteria 仍是标准英语复数，因此 criterias 是错误形式。

items.en: kritērion 'means of judging, standard' comes from kritēs 'judge', itself from krinein 'to separate, decide'. The suffix -ion marks an instrument or means.
items.cn: kritērion“判断工具、标准”来自 kritēs“法官”，后者又来自 krinein“分开、决定”。后缀 -ion 标记工具或手段。

items.en: Greek neuter nouns in -on form their plural in -a, so one kritērion becomes many kritēria. English kept this pattern: one criterion, two criteria.
items.cn: 以 -on 结尾的希腊中性名词复数作 -a，因此一个 kritērion 变多个 kritēria。英语保留这一模式：one criterion，two criteria。

items.en: Latin criterium and French critère transmitted the word; English criterion is recorded from the 17th century in logic and theology.
items.cn: 拉丁 criterium 与法语 critère 传递了这个词；英语 criterion 在17世纪的逻辑与神学文献中已有记录。

items.en: From the 19th century, criterion spread into medicine, engineering and law as a named test. Each field fixed its own set of criteria.
items.cn: 从19世纪起，criterion 作为具名检验标准扩展到医学、工程与法律。各领域固定了各自的 criteria。

items.en: The 20th century added criterion-referenced testing, where performance is judged against a stated standard rather than against other students.
items.cn: 20世纪新增 criterion-referenced testing（标准参照测评），按公布的标准而非按其他学生的相对位置评判表现。

items.en: The exact first English use of criterion is not certain, and the older anglicized plural criterions survives in a few technical texts. The deeper origin of krinein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: criterion 最早的确切英语用例不确定，英语化旧复数 criterions 仍见于少数技术文本。krinein 的更深来源属重构。

note.en: The first group is a set of singular/plural and spelling traps; the second contains near-synonyms that measure differently.
note.cn: 第一组是单复数与拼写陷阱；第二组是衡量方式不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The plural of criterion. It is often wrongly used as a singular, as in 'a criteria', which is nonstandard.
entries.definitionCN: criterion 的复数。常被误作单数使用，如 a criteria，属不规范。

entries.definition: A cycling race or a rare variant spelling; it is not the academic sense of criterion.
entries.definitionCN: 自行车绕圈赛，或罕见的异体拼写；不是 criterion 的学术义。

entries.definition: The judge who applies criteria; the criterion is the tool, the critic is the person.
entries.definitionCN: 应用标准进行判断的人；criterion 是工具，critic 是人。

entries.definition: A level of quality or a rule used for comparison; broader and less formal than criterion.
entries.definitionCN: 用于比较的质量水平或规则；比 criterion 更宽、更不正式。

entries.definition: A reference point used to compare performance; it is usually an achieved level, not a rule for judging.
entries.definitionCN: 用于比较表现的参照点；通常是已达成的水平，而非判断规则。

entries.definition: A means of measuring or assessing; it points to the act or unit of measurement rather than the principle.
entries.definitionCN: 测量或评估的手段；指向测量行为或单位，而非原则。

entries.definition: An informal standard for comparison; more figurative and conversational than criterion.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式的对比标准；比 criterion 更形象、更口语。

entries.definition: A procedure used to establish whether something meets a requirement; a criterion is the requirement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 用于确定某物是否达标的程序；criterion 是要求本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: genuine Greek morphology, fixed collocations and the real criterion family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊构词、固定搭配与真实的 criterion 词族。

normal.en: kritēs 'judge' + -ion 'means': a criterion is the judge's measuring tool.
normal.cn: kritēs“法官”+ -ion“工具”：criterion 就是法官的量尺。

normal.en: One criterion, two criteria: the Greek -on to -a shift is the same pattern as phenomenon to phenomena.
normal.cn: one criterion，two criteria：希腊语 -on 变 -a 的规则与 phenomenon 变 phenomena 相同。

normal.en: Learn selection criterion, meet the criteria and diagnostic criterion; they show the selection, research and medical branches.
normal.cn: 记住 selection criterion、meet the criteria、diagnostic criterion；它们展示选择、研究与医学分支。

normal.en: criterion, critic, critical, criticism and crisis all descend from krinein.
normal.cn: criterion、critic、critical、criticism、crisis 都出自 krinein。

normal.en: Never write criterias; if you need a plural, criteria is already it.
normal.cn: 绝不要写 criterias；需要复数时，criteria 本身就是复数。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across two job applications, deciding which one reaches the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子横在两份求职信上，决定哪一份够到刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a judge's desk with a single measuring rod, used for every case that comes before the court.
abstract.cn: 想象法官桌上只有一根量尺，用来衡量每一个上庭的案件。

abstract.en: Picture a rubric printed before an exam, so every student can see the same set of marks.
abstract.cn: 想象考试前印发的评分量规，让每个学生都看见同一套刻度。

examples.en: The committee set three criteria for evaluating the proposals.
examples.cn: 委员会为评估提案设定了三条标准。

examples.en: A good criterion is one that different judges can apply in the same way.
examples.cn: 好的标准是不同评判者都能以同样方式适用的标准。

examples.en: The new drug did not meet the safety criteria for approval.
examples.cn: 这种新药未达到批准所需的安全标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: “critic（评判者）+ erion（工具）”——评判者手里那把尺 → criterion 标准、准则（复数 criteria）

root: 希腊 kritērion“判断工具、标准”，来自 kritēs“法官”，再溯至 krinein“分开、决定”；-ion 表示工具或手段。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one object: a measuring tool held by a judge. The same tool measures merit, selects candidates, includes patients, decides cases, diagnoses disease, tests designs, separates truth, and awards marks.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一件物品：评判者手中的量具。同一件量具衡量优劣、筛选人选、纳入病例、裁断案件、诊断疾病、检验设计、分辨真假、给出分数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid across the options, marking the line they must reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子横在选项上，标出必须达到的刻度。

branches.en: TRUTH: testing a belief asks what standard makes the verdict stand.
branches.cn: 真理：检验信念要问什么标准能让结论站得住。

branches.en: SELECTION AND SCORING: choosing a site and awarding marks both apply a published line to candidates.
branches.cn: 选择与评分：选址与打分，都把一条公布的标准线应用到候选对象上。

branches.en: RESEARCH AND MEDICINE: inclusion criteria and diagnostic criteria make professional judgment repeatable.
branches.cn: 研究与医学：纳入标准与诊断标准让专业判断可重复。

branches.en: LAW AND ENGINEERING: a legal test and a design value both turn a principle into a measurable requirement.
branches.cn: 法律与工程：法律检验与设计数值，都把原则变成可测量的要求。

branches.en: THE TOOL ITSELF: a criterion is the instrument, not the act of judging or the person who judges.
branches.cn: 工具本身：criterion 是器具，不是判断行为，也不是判断者。

intro.en: Criterion is a Greek noun in -on, borrowed whole rather than built with English suffixes. Its plural -a is also Greek, which is why the form is irregular in English.
intro.cn: criterion 是以 -on 结尾的希腊名词，整体借入，并非用英语后缀构造。其复数 -a 也来自希腊语，因此该形式在英语中属不规则。
