latinIntro.en: Greek krinein 'to separate, decide' gives kritēs 'judge' and kritērion 'means of judging'. Latin kept criterion as a learned borrowing, and English took it from Latin rather than from Greek directly.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 krinein“分开、决定”给出 kritēs“法官”与 kritērion“判断工具”。拉丁语把 criterion 作为学术借词保留，英语是从拉丁语而非直接从希腊语借入的。

items.meaning: a standard or means of judging
items.meaningCN: 标准；判断工具（kritēs“法官”+ -ion“手段”）
items.example: Accuracy is the first criterion for a translation.
items.exampleCN: 准确是译文的第一个标准。

items.meaningCN: 两个或更多标准（希腊语 -on 变 -a 的复数）
items.example: The panel judged the entries against five criteria.
items.exampleCN: 评审团按五项标准评判参赛作品。

items.meaningCN: 评论家；批评者（经拉丁 criticus 来自 kritēs“法官”）
items.example: The critic applied the same criteria to every film.
items.exampleCN: 这位评论家用同样的标准评判每部影片。

items.meaningCN: 批判的；关键的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: The criterion is critical for a fair comparison.
items.exampleCN: 这一标准对公平比较至关重要。

items.meaningCN: 评判的实践（-ism 表实践）
items.example: The criteria shaped the criticism the work received.
items.exampleCN: 这些标准影响了该作品所受的评论。

items.meaningCN: 以评判的方式（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The proposal was critically assessed against the criteria.
items.exampleCN: 提案已对照标准作了批判性评估。

items.meaningCN: 决定性时刻；危机
items.example: The shortage reached crisis level.
items.exampleCN: 短缺达到了危机程度。

items.meaning: pretending to hold beliefs one lacks
items.meaningCN: 伪善（hypo-“在下”+ krinein“判断／演戏”）
items.example: The committee's hypocrisy was exposed by the audit.
items.exampleCN: 委员会的伪善被审计揭露。

items.meaning: tested against a stated standard rather than against peers
items.meaningCN: 标准参照的：按公布标准而非同伴相对位置测评
items.example: A criterion-referenced test reports whether each skill was met.
items.exampleCN: 标准参照测评报告每项技能是否达标。

latinEntries.meaning: a means or standard of judging

definition_en: increasing by successive additions, or resulting from a total built up over time
core_image: 沙漏下方的沙堆一层层加高
scene: The cumulative effect of small emissions became visible after a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 cumulative 是「累积的」（第 2 个义项：多次小影响累加成的总效应）；句意：微小排放的累积效应十年后才显现出来。图中可辨识物件：沙漏、逐年排放柱状图、上升曲线、工厂烟囱、十年刻度。

pos.zh: 累积的；渐增的；累计的（常作定语）

senses.title: Growing by successive additions
senses.titleCN: 逐次累加的：一层压一层地增长
senses.definition: increasing as each new amount is added to what already exists
senses.definitionCN: 随着每一新量加到既有数量上而增长
senses.example: The cumulative growth of the archive surprised the librarians.
senses.exampleCN: 档案的累积增长让馆员们感到意外。
senses.why: Latin cumulare means 'to heap up', from cumulus 'heap'. The adjective describes anything built by adding layer upon layer rather than by one jump.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 cumulare 意为“堆起”，来自 cumulus“堆”。这个形容词描述任何靠一层层添加、而非一步跳升而形成的事物。

senses.title: The total effect of many small causes
senses.titleCN: 累积效应：小事重复造成的总后果
senses.definition: describing an effect produced by repeated small causes acting over time
senses.definitionCN: 指由重复的小原因长期作用所产生的效应
senses.example: The cumulative effect of small emissions became visible after a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 微小排放的累积效应十年后才显现出来。
senses.why: A single small cause may be harmless, but heaping them together crosses a threshold, so the adjective names the total rather than any one item.
senses.whyCN: 单个小原因也许无害，但把它们堆起来就会越过某个阈值，因此这个形容词命名的是总体，而非任何单项。

senses.title: A running total in statistics
senses.titleCN: 累计数：统计里一路加下去的和
senses.definition: in statistics, describing a total formed by adding each value in turn
senses.definitionCN: 统计中把每个数值依次相加形成的总数
senses.example: The cumulative frequency column reaches one hundred per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 累积频数列最终达到百分之百。
senses.why: The statistical sense makes the heap exact: each row adds one more item to the pile, and the column shows the pile at every step.
senses.whyCN: 统计义把“堆”精确化：每一行往堆上再加一项，整列显示每一步的堆积高度。

senses.title: Cumulative evidence in law
senses.titleCN: 累积证据：多条单独不足、合起来有力
senses.definition: in law, describing separate pieces of evidence that strengthen one another when taken together
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指多条证据合在一起时互相增强
senses.example: The court admitted the records as cumulative evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院将这些记录作为累积证据采纳。
senses.why: Each item adds weight rather than replacing the others; the legal sense treats proof as a heap that grows heavier with every piece.
senses.whyCN: 每一项都在增加分量，而非替代其他项；法律义把证明看成一堆越加越重的东西。

senses.title: Cumulative interest or dividend
senses.titleCN: 累积利息／股息：未付部分滚存
senses.definition: in finance, describing interest or dividends that accumulate and must be paid later
senses.definitionCN: 金融中指利息或股息累积起来、须在以后支付
senses.example: The preferred shares carry cumulative dividends.
senses.exampleCN: 这些优先股带累积股息。
senses.why: Money that is not paid now is heaped onto the next payment, so the finance sense is the literal heap transferred from sand to unpaid amounts.
senses.whyCN: 现在未付的钱被堆到下一次支付上，因此金融义就是把沙堆的字面意象转移到未付金额。

senses.title: Lifetime accumulated risk
senses.titleCN: 累积风险：一生中反复暴露的总账
senses.definition: in medicine and public health, describing risk that adds up over repeated or prolonged exposure
senses.definitionCN: 医学与公共卫生中指重复或长期暴露累加起来的风险
senses.example: Cumulative exposure to sunlight raises the risk of skin damage.
senses.exampleCN: 长期累积的日晒会增加皮肤损伤风险。
senses.why: Risk is measured over a lifetime, not a single day: each exposure adds a small amount to the total, so the adjective marks the sum rather than the episode.
senses.whyCN: 风险按一生而非单日衡量：每次暴露都在总量上加一点，因此形容词标记的是总和，而非单次事件。

senses.title: Accumulated damage in materials
senses.titleCN: 累积损伤：材料一次次受载后的总损耗
senses.definition: in engineering, describing damage that builds up through repeated stress
senses.definitionCN: 工程中指反复受力逐步积累的损伤
senses.example: Engineers track cumulative damage in the turbine blades.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师追踪涡轮叶片的累积损伤。
senses.why: Materials do not fail from one load but from many; the adjective names the damage that has been heaped up beyond the visible single event.
senses.whyCN: 材料不是因一次载荷失效，而是因多次载荷失效；这个形容词命名的正是超出单次可见事件的堆积损伤。

senses.title: Cumulative culture
senses.titleCN: 累积文化：一代代叠加改进
senses.definition: in anthropology, describing knowledge or technology that improves through repeated additions across generations
senses.definitionCN: 人类学中指知识或技术经代际反复添补而改进
senses.example: Cumulative culture allows each generation to start from earlier tools.
senses.exampleCN: 累积文化让每一代人都从更早的工具出发。
senses.why: Culture is a heap that never resets: each generation adds a small improvement and passes the larger pile on, which is why human technology can outrun individual invention.
senses.whyCN: 文化是一堆不会清零的东西：每代添一点改进，再把更大的堆传下去，这正是人类技术能超越个人发明的原因。

intro.en: Cumulative is cumul- + -ive, from Latin cumulare 'to heap up'. The same stem gives accumulate and the cloud name cumulus, both built on the image of a pile.
intro.cn: cumulative 是 cumul- + -ive，来自拉丁 cumulare“堆起”。同一词干还产生 accumulate 与云名 cumulus，二者都建立在“堆”的意象上。

items.en: cumulus meant 'a heap, mass or pile'. It was used of piled earth or grain and later gave the meteorological term for heaped clouds.
items.cn: cumulus 意为“堆、堆块”。它曾用于堆起的土或谷物，后来产生指堆状云的气象术语。

items.en: cumulare 'to heap up, amass' was formed from cumulus. Its past participle cumulatus supplies the stem cumulat- used in English.
items.cn: cumulare“堆起、积聚”由 cumulus 构成。其过去分词 cumulatus 提供英语使用的词干 cumulat-。

items.en: The suffix -ive, from Latin -ivus 'having the nature of', makes an adjective of tendency: cumulative describes what tends to heap up or what results from heaping.
items.cn: 后缀 -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus“具有……性质的”，构成表倾向的形容词：cumulative 描述倾向于堆积的事物，或由堆积产生的结果。

items.en: English cumulative appears in the 17th century, first in learned and legal writing about totals and evidence. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 cumulative 于17世纪出现，最早见于讨论总数与证据的学术和法律文本。年代为约数。

items.en: Statistics, finance, medicine and engineering each adopted the word for their own running totals in the 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 统计学、金融、医学与工程分别在19、20世纪采用这个词来表示各自的累计总量。

items.en: The deeper origin of Latin cumulus is uncertain; it is often treated as a derivative of a root meaning 'heap', but no single reconstruction is agreed. Exact English dates are approximate.
items.cn: 拉丁 cumulus 的更深来源不确定；常被视为某个意为“堆”的词根的派生，但没有公认的单一重构。英语确切年代为约数。

note.en: The first group contains look-alike words from different roots; the second contains words for totals and growth that count differently.
note.cn: 第一组是来自不同词根的形近词；第二组是计算方式不同的“总量／增长”类词。

entries.definition: Tending to accumulate; it stresses the habit or process of collecting, while cumulative usually describes the resulting total.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于积累的；强调收集的习惯或过程，而 cumulative 通常描述形成的总量。

entries.definition: A heap-shaped cloud; the noun names the pile itself, not the process of adding to it.
entries.definitionCN: 积云；这个名词命名堆本身，而非堆积过程。

entries.definition: Relating to a climax or highest point, from Latin culmen 'top'. It looks like cumulative but has no heap in it.
entries.definitionCN: 与顶点、高潮有关的，来自拉丁 culmen“顶”。它形似 cumulative，但词源里没有“堆”。

entries.definition: Already gathered into a store; it describes the completed stock, while cumulative describes the adding process or its pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 已经聚集起来的；描述完成的存量，而 cumulative 描述添加过程或其模式。

entries.definition: A total formed by combining separate items; it does not imply growth over time.
entries.definitionCN: 由各项合并而成的总数；不暗示随时间增长。

entries.definition: Increasing by small steps; it stresses the size of each step, while cumulative stresses the total reached.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步小幅增加的；强调每步的幅度，而 cumulative 强调达到的总量。

entries.definition: Shared by or belonging to a group; it is about ownership or joint action, not heaping over time.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共享或属于群体的；关乎归属或共同行动，而非长期堆积。

entries.definition: Continuing step by step over time; it can describe growth but not necessarily a total.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间逐步持续的；可描述增长，但不必形成总量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, fixed collocations and the genuine cumulus family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、固定搭配与真实的 cumulus 词族。

normal.en: cumulus 'heap' + -ive: the adjective describes whatever is formed by heaping.
normal.cn: cumulus“堆”+ -ive：这个形容词描述一切靠堆积形成的东西。

normal.en: accumulate and cumulative share the same heap, one as a verb and one as an adjective.
normal.cn: accumulate 与 cumulative 共享同一个“堆”，一个是动词，一个是形容词。

normal.en: Learn cumulative effect, cumulative total and cumulative evidence; these are the three most common academic uses.
normal.cn: 记住 cumulative effect、cumulative total、cumulative evidence；这是三个最常见的学术用法。

normal.en: cumulus clouds are heaps of cloud, which is the same picture as a cumulative total.
normal.cn: cumulus 云就是堆状的云，与累计总数的画面相同。

normal.en: Do not confuse cumulative with culminative: one heaps, the other reaches a top.
normal.cn: 不要把 cumulative 与 culminative 混淆：一个是堆，一个是到达顶点。

abstract.en: Picture sand falling through an hourglass, each grain adding to one growing cone.
abstract.cn: 想象沙粒穿过沙漏，每一粒都加到一个不断长高的圆锥上。

abstract.en: Picture a wall built one brick per day until it is thick enough to change the weather behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象每天只砌一块砖的墙，直到厚到足以改变墙后的天气。

abstract.en: Picture an interest ledger where unpaid amounts roll into the next row and grow larger each time.
abstract.cn: 想象一本利息账簿，未付金额滚入下一行，每次都变得更大。

examples.en: The cumulative total of donations passed one million dollars.
examples.cn: 捐款累计总额超过了一百万美元。

examples.en: Repeated small delays had a cumulative effect on the schedule.
examples.cn: 反复的小延误对进度产生了累积效应。

examples.en: The report assesses the cumulative impact of tourism on the coast.
examples.cn: 报告评估了旅游业对海岸的累积影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: “Q（cu）mulate（堆）”——像 Q 一样一圈圈堆上去 → cumulative 累积的、渐增的

root: 拉丁 cumulus“堆、堆块”→ cumulare“堆起、积聚”→ cumulat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one image: a heap that grows by addition. The heap may be sand, data, evidence, unpaid interest, exposure, damage or cultural knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个意象：靠添加而增高的堆。这堆东西可以是沙、数据、证据、未付利息、暴露量、损伤或文化知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cone of sand growing grain by grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙粒逐颗落下、不断长高的圆锥。

branches.en: ADDING: successive growth and a statistical running total are the same addition seen qualitatively and numerically.
branches.cn: 添加：逐次增长与统计累计数，是同一加法在性质与数量两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: THRESHOLD DAMAGE: small causes and repeated stress both become serious only after the heap is large enough.
branches.cn: 阈值损伤：小原因与反复应力，都要等堆足够大才变得严重。

branches.en: LAW AND FINANCE: separate evidence and unpaid dividends both add weight or value without replacing the earlier items.
branches.cn: 法律与金融：分散证据与未付股息都在增加分量或价值，而不取代先前项目。

branches.en: LIFETIME EXPOSURE: risk adds up across many episodes, so the total matters more than any single exposure.
branches.cn: 终生暴露：风险在多次事件中累加，因此总量比任何单次暴露更重要。

branches.en: CULTURE: improvements accumulate across generations, making the heap inherited rather than personal.
branches.cn: 文化：改进在代际间累积，使这堆东西成为继承物而非个人成就。

intro.en: Cumulative is a Latin adjective in -ive built on the participle stem cumulat-. The related verb accumulate adds the prefix ad- to the same base.
intro.cn: cumulative 是建立在分词词干 cumulat- 上的拉丁 -ive 形容词。相关动词 accumulate 在同一词基上加前缀 ad-。

latinIntro.en: Latin cumulus 'heap' gives cumulare 'to heap up' and the adjective cumulativus. English borrowed the stem as cumulat- and added -ive, while accumulate came through the prefixed form accumulare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cumulus“堆”产生 cumulare“堆起”与形容词 cumulativus。英语借入词干 cumulat- 并加 -ive，而 accumulate 经带前缀形式 accumulare 进入。

items.meaning: tending to heap up; formed by accumulation
items.meaningCN: 累积的；渐增的（cumulat- + -ive 表倾向）
items.example: The cumulative effect was larger than expected.
items.exampleCN: 累积效应比预期更大。

items.meaningCN: 积累；堆积（ad-“向”+ cumulare“堆”）
items.example: Dust accumulated on the shelves.
items.exampleCN: 灰尘在架子上积了起来。

items.meaning: a mass that has been gathered
items.meaningCN: 积累物；堆积（-ion 结果名词）
items.example: The accumulation of sediment blocked the channel.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物堆积堵塞了水道。

items.meaning: by adding one item to another
items.meaningCN: 累积地；渐增地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: Cumulatively, the changes altered the whole system.
items.exampleCN: 这些变化累积起来改变了整个系统。

items.meaningCN: 堆；积云
items.example: Cumulus clouds formed above the hills.
items.exampleCN: 山丘上方形成了积云。

items.meaning: a device that stores energy or data
items.meaningCN: 蓄电池；累加器（-or 表装置）
items.example: The accumulator stores charge between cycles.
items.exampleCN: 蓄电池在循环之间储存电荷。

items.meaning: a running count of values up to a point
items.meaningCN: 累积频数（逐项累加的计数）
items.example: The cumulative frequency rises steadily across the table.
items.exampleCN: 累积频数在整张表中稳步上升。

items.meaning: separate proofs that reinforce one another
items.meaningCN: 互相增强的累积证据
items.example: The judge described the letters as cumulative evidence.
items.exampleCN: 法官把这些信件称为累积证据。

items.meaning: tending to collect or pile up
items.meaningCN: 倾向于积累的（-ive 表倾向）
items.example: The accumulative habit of note-taking paid off.
items.exampleCN: 做笔记的积累习惯最终有了回报。

definition_en: at the present time, or in the present state of affairs
core_image: 河水正穿过一座标着“现在”的桥洞
scene: The building is currently under renovation.
sceneCN: 这里 currently 是「目前、正在」（第 4 个义项：处于当前进行状态）；句意：这栋楼目前正在翻修。图中可辨识物件：施工围挡、脚手架、施工告示牌、时钟、翻修中的楼体。

pos.zh: 目前；当前；眼下（修饰状态、职位、进程）

forms.label: 无比较级（时间副词，一般不用比较级）
forms.form: currently（需要对比时用 at present / now 等表达）

derivatives.zh: 当前的；流通的；水流；电流

senses.title: At the present time
senses.titleCN: 目前：以说话时为参照的现在
senses.definition: at the present time, as opposed to the past or a possible future
senses.definitionCN: 在当前时间，相对于过去或可能的未来
senses.example: The museum is currently closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆目前因维修关闭。
senses.why: current comes from Latin currere 'to run': the present is the moment now running. The adverb marks whatever is true at this running moment.
senses.whyCN: current 来自拉丁 currere“跑”：现在就是正在奔跑的这一刻。这个副词标记的是在这一刻为真的事。

senses.title: At the moment of speaking
senses.titleCN: 此刻：说话这一瞬间
senses.definition: at the exact moment of speaking or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作的这一确切瞬间
senses.example: I am currently reading a history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 我此刻正在读一本关于这座城市的史书。
senses.why: The deictic 'now' is fixed by the speaker's moment. Using currently instead of now sounds more formal and often implies an ongoing activity.
senses.whyCN: 指示性的“现在”由说话者的时刻确定。用 currently 而非 now 更正式，且常暗示活动正在进行。

senses.title: Now, in contrast with the past
senses.titleCN: 如今：与过去对照的现在
senses.definition: in the present period, especially when contrasting it with an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 在当前时期，尤用于与更早时期对照
senses.example: The factory once employed two thousand workers; it currently employs four hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂曾雇两千名工人，目前只雇四百人。
senses.why: A running river never stands still, so 'current' naturally sets the present against earlier stretches of the same flow: formerly one state, currently another.
senses.whyCN: 奔流的河水从不停住，因此 current 自然把现在与同一流程中更早的一段对照起来：从前一种状态，目前另一种状态。

senses.title: In the present state or process
senses.titleCN: 正在：处于当前进程之中
senses.definition: in the state or process that is going on at present
senses.definitionCN: 处于当前正在进行的状态或过程
senses.example: The building is currently under renovation.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼目前正在翻修。
senses.why: This sense points to an unfinished process rather than a date. The matter is still running, so currently means 'in mid-course'.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项指向未完成的过程，而非日期。事情仍在运行，所以 currently 意为“进行中”。

senses.title: Holding a post at present
senses.titleCN: 现任：当前担任某职
senses.definition: holding an office or position at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 目前担任某一职务或职位
senses.example: She is currently serving as interim director.
senses.exampleCN: 她目前担任临时主任。
senses.why: A post is a stretch of time a person is running through. Currently marks the part of that stretch which includes now, without promising how long it lasts.
senses.whyCN: 职位是一段个人正在跑过的时间。currently 标记这段中包含现在的部分，不承诺它持续多久。

senses.title: Available at present
senses.titleCN: 目前可得的：按现状可获得
senses.definition: available, in stock or on offer at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 目前可获得的、有货的或在售的
senses.example: Only two models are currently available.
senses.exampleCN: 目前只有两款有货。
senses.why: Commercial statements are dated by the moment of the offer: what is on the shelf now may not be next month, so currently limits the claim to the present state.
senses.whyCN: 商业陈述以报价时刻为界：现在货架上的东西下月未必还在，因此 currently 把陈述限定在当前状态。

senses.title: In present-day knowledge or usage
senses.titleCN: 在当前认识／用法中
senses.definition: according to the present state of knowledge, practice or wording
senses.definitionCN: 按照当前的知识、实践或措辞状态
senses.example: The method is currently regarded as the standard treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 该方法目前被视为标准疗法。
senses.why: Scholarship also runs forward: a view accepted now may be revised later. Currently admits that limit and marks the claim as time-bound.
senses.whyCN: 学术也在向前跑：现在接受的看法以后可能被修正。currently 承认这一限制，把陈述标记为受时间约束。

senses.title: At this stage of a sequence
senses.titleCN: 当前阶段：流程走到的那一步
senses.definition: at the stage that a process has reached so far
senses.definitionCN: 某个流程迄今所到达的阶段
senses.example: The application is currently at the interview stage.
senses.exampleCN: 申请目前处于面试阶段。
senses.why: A process is a course that runs stage by stage. Currently names the stage now being run, leaving the remaining stages open.
senses.whyCN: 流程是一段逐段推进的行程。currently 命名的是正在跑的那一段，其余阶段仍敞开。

intro.en: Currently is current + -ly. Current comes from Latin currere 'to run' through Old French, so the word's core image is something flowing at this moment.
intro.cn: currently 是 current + -ly。current 经古法语来自拉丁 currere“跑”，因此这个词的核心意象是此刻正在流动的东西。

items.en: currere meant 'to run, flow'. Its present participle currens 'running' is the source of the adjective current, literally 'that which runs'.
items.cn: currere 意为“跑、流动”。其现在分词 currens“正在跑的”就是形容词 current 的来源，字面即“正在流动的”。

items.en: Old French corant 'running, flowing' passed into Middle English as current. The spelling with -ur- reflects the Latin stem rather than the French form.
items.cn: 古法语 corant“奔跑的、流动的”进入中古英语作 current。拼写中的 -ur- 反映拉丁词干，而非法语形式。

items.en: From 'running water' the word extended to 'the present course of time', giving phrases such as the current year and current events. The adverb follows.
items.cn: 从“流动的水”扩展到“当前的时间进程”，产生 the current year、current events 等说法。副词随后出现。

items.en: current + -ly (Old English -lice) makes an adverb meaning 'in the current state'. English -ly adverbs commonly modify whole states, not only actions.
items.cn: current + -ly（古英语 -lice）构成意为“处于当前状态”的副词。英语 -ly 副词常修饰整个状态，而不只是动作。

items.en: In modern formal writing currently replaces now and at present, especially in reports, job titles and status updates. Its exact first use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 在现代正式写作中，currently 替代 now 与 at present，尤见于报告、职位与状态说明。其最早用例没有确切年代。

items.en: The deeper origin of Latin currere is a reconstruction. The precise date when currently became common in commercial and academic prose is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁 currere 的更深来源属重构。currently 在商业与学术文章中普及的确切年代存疑。

note.en: The first group contains look-alike time words and one false friend; the second contains synonyms with different degrees of formality or time reference.
note.cn: 第一组是形近时间词与一个假朋友；第二组是正式程度或时间指向不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The base word: an adjective meaning 'present' or a noun meaning a flow of water, air or electricity.
entries.definitionCN: 词基：形容词“当前的”，或名词“水流、气流、电流”。

entries.definition: A small dried grape or the shrub that bears it, named after Corinth. It has nothing to do with time or running.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小葡萄干或结这种果实的灌木，得名于科林斯。与时间或奔跑毫无关系。

entries.definition: Money in circulation, or the state of being accepted; from the same 'flowing' root but a different noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 流通中的货币，或被普遍接受的状态；同出“流动”词根，但名词义不同。

entries.definition: In British English usually 'now'; in American English often 'soon'. Currently avoids that ambiguity.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语通常指“现在”，美式英语常指“很快”。currently 避免了这种歧义。

entries.definition: The plain adverb for the present moment; it is less formal and less likely to describe an institutional status.
entries.definitionCN: 表示此刻的普通副词；更不正式，较少用于描述机构状态。

entries.definition: A formal phrase meaning 'now'; it is close to currently but can sound more contrastive with the past.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的“目前”短语；与 currently 接近，但与过去的对照意味更强。

entries.definition: In these times generally; it covers a whole era rather than a specific current state.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指当今时代；覆盖整个时期，而非具体当前状态。

entries.definition: For a moment, or in American English 'very soon'; it concerns brevity or imminence, not the present state.
entries.definitionCN: 片刻地，或美式英语中“马上”；关乎短暂或迫近，而非当前状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: genuine morphology, standard collocations and the real currere family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、标准搭配与真实的 currere 词族。

normal.en: currere 'to run': the present is the moment that is running now, so currently means 'at this running moment'.
normal.cn: currere“跑”：现在就是此刻正在奔跑的时刻，所以 currently 意为“在这一奔跑的当下”。

normal.en: current + -ly: the adjective of present state becomes an adverb of present state.
normal.cn: current + -ly：表当前状态的形容词变成表当前状态的副词。

normal.en: Learn currently under review, currently available and currently serving as; these cover process, stock and office.
normal.cn: 记住 currently under review、currently available、currently serving as；分别覆盖进程、存货与职位。

normal.en: course, occur, currency and current all come from currere, the running root.
normal.cn: course、occur、currency、current 都来自 currere 这个“跑”的词根。

normal.en: currant is not current: one is a grape, the other is time.
normal.cn: currant 不是 current：一个是葡萄干，一个是时间。

abstract.en: Picture a river passing under a bridge marked 'now'; everything upstream is the past, everything downstream the future.
abstract.cn: 想象河水穿过一座标着“现在”的桥；上游是过去，下游是未来。

abstract.en: Picture a progress bar with one segment lit: that lit segment is what currently means.
abstract.cn: 想象进度条上亮着的一段：currently 指的就是亮着的那一段。

abstract.en: Picture a job title card that can be replaced tomorrow, showing how 'current' claims are time-stamped.
abstract.cn: 想象一张明天就可能被换掉的职位牌，显示“当前”陈述都带有时间戳。

examples.en: The position is currently held by a visiting professor.
examples.cn: 该职位目前由一位访问教授担任。

examples.en: The committee is currently reviewing all applications.
examples.cn: 委员会目前正在审查所有申请。

examples.en: Currently, the evidence does not support either explanation.
examples.cn: 目前，证据不支持两种解释中的任何一种。

dict_mnemonic.text: “current（水流）+ ly”——水流到眼前这一刻 → currently 目前、当前

root: 拉丁 currere“跑、流动”→ 现在分词 currens“正在流动的”→ 古法语 corant → 英语 current + -ly 副词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one deictic centre: the moment now running. The adverb can mark a time, a process, a post, an availability, a state of knowledge or a stage in a sequence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个指示中心：此刻正在运行的这一刻。副词可标记时间、进程、职位、可得性、认识状态或序列中的阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water flowing through the arch of the present moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：水流穿过“此刻”的桥洞。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: general present time and the exact instant of speaking are the same deictic centre at two precisions.
branches.cn: 时刻：一般现在时间与说话的确切瞬间，是同一指示中心在两种精度上的呈现。

branches.en: CONTRAST WITH AN EARLIER STATE: today’s factory sets the present against a former one.
branches.cn: 与早先状态对照：今天的工厂把现在与从前并置。

branches.en: PROCESS AND STAGE: a renovation and a job application are both unfinished courses with a lit segment.
branches.cn: 进程与阶段：翻修与求职申请都是未完成的行程，都有一段亮着。

branches.en: OFFICE AND STOCK: a current director and currently available models both hold only for the present state.
branches.cn: 职位与存货：现任主任与当前有货的型号，都只在当前状态下成立。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: currently frames a scholarly claim as provisional, open to later revision.
branches.cn: 认识：currently 把学术主张框定为暂定，日后可被修正。

intro.en: Currently is current + -ly. Current itself is a Latin participle stem that entered English through French, so the word combines a borrowed adjective with a native adverb suffix.
intro.cn: currently 是 current + -ly。current 本身是经法语进入英语的拉丁分词词干，因此这个词是借入形容词加本族副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin currere 'to run' yields currens 'running', cursus 'a course' and the prefixed forms occurrere, recurrere and incurrere. English keeps curr- in current, currency, course, occur, recur and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 currere“跑”产生 currens“正在跑的”、cursus“行程”，以及带前缀的 occurrere、recurrere、incurrere。英语在 current、currency、course、occur、recur、excursion 中保留 curr-。

items.meaningCN: 目前；当前（-ly 状态副词）
items.example: The site is currently unavailable.
items.exampleCN: 该网站目前无法访问。

items.meaning: present; a flow of water, air or electricity
items.meaningCN: 当前的；水流、气流、电流
items.example: The current carries sediment downstream.
items.exampleCN: 水流把沉积物带向下游。

items.meaningCN: 流通货币；通用、流行（-cy 状态名词）
items.example: The currency lost half its value.
items.exampleCN: 该货币贬值一半。

items.meaning: a route or sequence; a unit of study
items.meaningCN: 行程；路线；课程
items.example: The river changed course after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水后河流改变了流向。

items.meaning: to happen, to come to mind

items.example: The class took an excursion to the museum.

items.example: The curriculum was revised last year.

definition_en: the process of reaching a conclusion by reasoning, or an amount taken away from a total
core_image: 一条长链从一般前提一路扣到最后一块
scene: The tax deduction lowered her annual bill by two thousand dollars.
sceneCN: 这里 deduction 是「扣除额、税收扣除」（第 4 个义项：可从应税收入中减去的款项）；句意：这项税收扣除让她的年度税单少了两千美元。图中可辨识物件：税表、计算器、减号、收据、年度账单。

pos.zh: 推论；演绎（不可数）；结论（可数）；扣除；扣除额

senses.title: Reasoning from the general to the particular
senses.titleCN: 演绎推理：从通则推到个案
senses.definition: the process of drawing a particular conclusion from general premises
senses.definitionCN: 从一般前提出发得出特定结论的过程
senses.example: The argument proceeds by deduction from two general principles.
senses.exampleCN: 该论证从两条一般原则出发，通过演绎推进。
senses.why: Latin deducere means 'to lead away or down'. Reasoning is pictured as leading a conclusion down from higher premises to the case at hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 deducere 意为“引开、引下”。推理被描绘成把结论从更高的前提一路引到眼前个案。

senses.title: The conclusion reached
senses.titleCN: 推出的结论：演绎的产物
senses.definition: the particular conclusion that results from such reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 由这种推理得出的特定结论
senses.example: Her deduction surprised the investigators.
senses.exampleCN: 她推出的结论让调查人员吃惊。
senses.why: The act and its product share one noun: what is led down is both the leading and the thing that arrives at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 行为与产物共用同一个名词：被引下来的既是“引”的过程，也是最终抵达下面的那个东西。

senses.title: Subtraction in arithmetic
senses.titleCN: 减法：从总数里减去
senses.definition: the arithmetic operation of taking one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数中减去另一个数的算术运算
senses.example: The final step is a simple deduction of five from the total.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一步是从总数中减去五。
senses.why: The same 'lead away' image works for numbers: an amount is led away from the total, leaving a smaller figure behind.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“引开”意象也适用于数字：一笔数额被从总数中引走，留下更小的数。

senses.title: A tax deduction
senses.titleCN: 税收扣除：从应税收入中减去
senses.definition: an amount allowed to be subtracted from taxable income
senses.definitionCN: 允许从应税收入中减去的款项
senses.example: The tax deduction lowered her annual bill by two thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税收扣除让她的年度税单少了两千美元。
senses.why: Tax law leads certain expenses away from income before the rate is applied, so the amount is literally deducted from the taxable base.
senses.whyCN: 税法在适用税率前把某些支出从收入中引走，因此这笔款项确实是从应税基数中扣除的。

senses.title: A payroll deduction
senses.titleCN: 工资扣款：发薪前先扣走
senses.definition: an amount withheld from wages before payment
senses.definitionCN: 发薪前从工资中预先扣下的款项
senses.example: The payslip lists three deductions, including pension contributions.
senses.exampleCN: 工资单列出三项扣款，包括养老金缴款。
senses.why: The employer leads money away from gross pay before the worker receives it. The noun names both the act and the sum withheld.
senses.whyCN: 雇主在工人拿到工资前把钱从应发额中引走。这个名词既指行为，也指被扣下的金额。

senses.title: The act of subtracting
senses.titleCN: 扣除行为：减法这个动作本身
senses.definition: the act of taking something away from a whole or an amount
senses.definitionCN: 从整体或数额中拿走某物的行为
senses.example: The deduction of the agency fee happens at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 代理费的扣除在月底进行。
senses.why: When the focus is on the operation rather than the sum, deduction names the taking-away itself, parallel to subtraction as an activity.
senses.whyCN: 当焦点在操作而非金额时，deduction 命名的是“拿走”本身，与作为活动的 subtraction 平行。

senses.title: The deductive method
senses.titleCN: 演绎法：以演绎为主的推理方式
senses.definition: a method of inquiry that works from general theory to specific predictions
senses.definitionCN: 从一般理论推出具体预测的研究方法
senses.example: The course contrasts the deductive and inductive methods.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程对比演绎法与归纳法。
senses.why: Deduction as a method is reasoning treated as a procedure: start at the general level and lead the conclusion down to the data.
senses.whyCN: 作为方法的演绎，是把推理当作程序：从一般层面出发，把结论一路引到数据。

senses.title: A price reduction
senses.titleCN: 减价：从标价中减去的部分
senses.definition: an amount taken off a price or quoted sum
senses.definitionCN: 从价格或报价中减去的数额
senses.example: The dealer offered a deduction of five per cent for cash payment.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商对现金付款提供了百分之五的减价。
senses.why: Commerce leads a part of the quoted price away as an allowance, so the word covers discounts as well as tax and wage deductions.
senses.whyCN: 商业把报价的一部分作为让利引走，因此这个词也覆盖折扣，不只税收与工资扣款。

intro.en: Deduction comes from Latin deductio 'a leading away', from deducere 'to lead down or away'. The logical sense is a later, figurative extension of a physical leading.
intro.cn: deduction 来自拉丁 deductio“引开”，源自 deducere“引下、引走”。逻辑义是物理“引导”意象后来的比喻延伸。

items.en: deducere joins de- 'down, away' with ducere 'to lead'. Its literal picture is leading someone or something from one place to another, often downhill.
items.cn: deducere 由 de-“向下、离开”与 ducere“引导”组成。其字面画面是把人或物从一处引到另一处，常含向下之意。

items.en: deductio 'a leading away' covered both physical escorting and, in rhetorical and legal writing, the drawing out of an argument.
items.cn: deductio“引开”既指实际的护送，也指修辞与法律写作中对论点的引出。

items.en: Medieval and early modern logic used the Latin word for drawing a conclusion from premises; English deduction took this sense in the 16th century. The exact route is roughly dated.
items.cn: 中世纪与近代早期逻辑学用这个拉丁词表示从前提引出结论；英语 deduction 在16世纪取得此义。具体路径年代为约数。

items.en: The sense 'subtraction' and later 'amount subtracted' developed in parallel, since taking a number away is also a leading away. Tax and wage uses are modern extensions.
items.cn: “减法”义及后来的“扣除额”义平行发展，因为拿走一个数字同样是“引开”。税收与工资用法是现代的延伸。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries deduction became the standard name for the general-to-particular method, opposed to induction.
items.cn: 19、20世纪，deduction 成为“从一般到个别”方法的标准名称，与 induction（归纳）相对。

items.en: The precise date when the logical sense entered English is uncertain, and the deeper PIE origin of ducere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 逻辑义进入英语的确切年代存疑，ducere 的更早印欧语来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains related forms that differ in part of speech or prefix; the second contains reasoning and subtraction terms with different directions.
note.cn: 第一组是词性或前缀不同的相关形式；第二组是方向不同的推理与减法术语。

entries.definition: The adjective describing reasoning of this kind; deduction is the noun for the process or result.
entries.definitionCN: 描述这类推理的形容词；deduction 是过程或结果的名词。

entries.definition: To subtract an amount; it is the verb used for tax and wages, not for logical inference.
entries.definitionCN: 减去一笔金额；用于税收与工资，不用于逻辑推断。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion by reasoning; it is the verb that pairs with deduction in the logical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 通过推理得出结论；与逻辑义的 deduction 搭配的动词。

entries.definition: Any conclusion drawn from evidence; it covers both deduction and induction, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据得出的任何结论；同时覆盖演绎与归纳，因此更宽。

entries.definition: The end point of an argument; it names the result, while deduction can name the process too.
entries.definitionCN: 论证的终点；命名的结果，而 deduction 也可命名过程。

entries.definition: The arithmetic operation of taking one number from another; it lacks the logical and financial senses.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个数减去另一个数的算术运算；没有逻辑与金融义。

entries.definition: A partial refund paid back after a payment; a deduction is taken off before payment.
entries.definitionCN: 付款后返还的部分款项；deduction 是付款前先减去。

entries.definition: An amount allowed for a purpose; in tax contexts it functions like a deduction but stresses permission.
entries.definitionCN: 为某用途允许的额度；在税务语境中作用类似扣除，但强调“允许”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, standard collocations and the ducere word family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、标准搭配与 ducere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'down/away' + ducere 'lead': a deduction leads the conclusion down from general premises.
normal.cn: de-“向下／离开”+ ducere“引导”：deduction 把结论从一般前提引下来。

normal.en: The same 'lead away' image gives the money sense: an amount is led away from the total.
normal.cn: 同一个“引开”意象给出金钱义：一笔数额被从总数中引走。

normal.en: Learn tax deduction, logical deduction and payroll deduction; these show the three main branches.
normal.cn: 记住 tax deduction、logical deduction、payroll deduction；它们展示三个主要分支。

normal.en: deduce is for logic, deduct is for money: keep the pair apart.
normal.cn: deduce 用于逻辑，deduct 用于金钱：把这组分开。

normal.en: deduction, deductive, deduce, deduct and duct all carry the duc- 'lead' core.
normal.cn: deduction、deductive、deduce、deduct、duct 都带有 duc-“引导”核心。

abstract.en: Picture a chain pulled down from a high hook, each link a premise, ending at one small conclusion.
abstract.cn: 想象一条链从高处钩子被拉下，每一环是一个前提，末端是一个小结论。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of coins with one coin slid off the edge: subtraction is the same leading away.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠硬币中有一枚被滑出边缘：减法就是同一种“引开”。

abstract.en: Picture a payslip with three lines struck out before the final figure is printed.
abstract.cn: 想象工资单上在最终数字打印前划掉三行。

examples.en: From the two premises, the detective made a deduction about the time of the crime.
examples.cn: 侦探从两个前提推断出作案时间。

examples.en: The standard deduction reduces the income on which tax is calculated.
examples.cn: 标准扣除额减少了计税所依据的收入。

examples.en: A deduction of ten per cent applies to orders paid in advance.
examples.cn: 预付订单可享受百分之十的减价。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（向下）+ duc（引导）+ tion”——把结论从上往下引出来，也把钱从总数里引走 → deduction 推论、扣除

root: 拉丁 deducere“引下、引走”（de-“向下／离开”+ ducere“引导”）；deduct- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture: leading something away. Logic leads a conclusion down from premises; arithmetic, tax and payroll lead an amount away from a total.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：把某物引开。逻辑把结论从前提引下；算术、税收与工资则把一笔数额从总数引走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain pulled down from a high point to a single end link.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条链从高处被拉下，最后落到单独一环。

branches.en: LOGIC: reasoning from premises and the deductive method are the same downward leading, one as an act and one as a procedure.
branches.cn: 逻辑：从前提推理与演绎法，是同一种向下引导，一个是行为，一个是程序。

branches.en: RESULT: the conclusion is what arrives at the bottom of the chain.
branches.cn: 结果：结论就是抵达链条底端的东西。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: subtraction and the act of subtracting are the same taking-away seen as operation and activity.
branches.cn: 算术：减法与扣除行为，是同一“拿走”在运算与活动两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: MONEY: tax deductions and payroll deductions both lead an amount away before the final figure is fixed.
branches.cn: 金钱：税收扣除与工资扣款，都在最终数字确定前把一笔金额引走。

branches.en: PRICE: a deduction from a quoted price is the same allowance applied at the point of sale.
branches.cn: 价格：从报价中减去的部分，是在销售环节应用的同一让利。

intro.en: Deduction is deduct + -ion, on the Latin participle stem deduct-. The base verb is deducere; the prefix de- and the root duc- are fossilized inside it.
intro.cn: deduction 是 deduct + -ion，建立在拉丁分词词干 deduct- 上。词基动词是 deducere；前缀 de- 与词根 duc- 已凝固在其内部。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'to lead' yields a large family: conduct, produce, reduce, introduce, induce, educate and deduct. The prefixed forms each specify a direction of leading.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”衍生出庞大词族：conduct、produce、reduce、introduce、induce、educate、deduct。每个带前缀形式都指定一种引导方向。

items.meaning: a leading away; a conclusion or an amount removed
items.meaningCN: 引开；推论；扣除（-ion 名词后缀）
items.example: The deduction follows from the second premise.
items.exampleCN: 这个推论由第二个前提得出。

items.meaning: to reach a conclusion by reasoning
items.meaningCN: 推断；演绎（de-“向下”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: We can deduce the age of the rock from its layers.
items.exampleCN: 我们可以从岩层推断岩石的年龄。

items.meaningCN: 扣除；减去（de-“离开”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The fee is deducted from the first payment.
items.exampleCN: 费用从首笔付款中扣除。

items.meaning: relating to reasoning from general to particular
items.meaningCN: 演绎的（-ive 表性质）
items.example: The deductive step is valid but the premise is false.
items.exampleCN: 演绎步骤有效，但前提是假的。

items.meaning: able to be subtracted; an amount paid before insurance covers the rest
items.meaningCN: 可扣除的；保险免赔额（-ible“可……的”）
items.example: The policy has a five-hundred-dollar deductible.
items.exampleCN: 该保单有五百美元免赔额。

items.meaningCN: 可推断的（-ible“可……的”）
items.example: The conclusion is deducible from the data.
items.exampleCN: 该结论可从数据推断出来。

items.meaning: to lead into a state or belief
items.meaningCN: 诱导；引起（in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The drug induces sleep within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这种药几分钟内就能引起睡意。

items.meaning: to lead back; to make smaller
items.meaningCN: 减少；使变小（re-“回”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The new rules reduced waste by a third.
items.exampleCN: 新规定使浪费减少了三分之一。

items.meaning: to lead or guide; to carry out
items.meaningCN: 引导；进行（con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: She conducted the experiment twice.
items.exampleCN: 她把实验做了两次。

latinEntries.meaning: a leading away; a drawing out

definition_zh: 演绎的；推论的；从一般到个别的
definition_en: relating to reasoning that moves from general premises to a particular conclusion
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌从宽大底座一路推到最后一张小牌
scene: The detective's method was deductive: he began with a general rule and narrowed it to one suspect.
sceneCN: 这里 deductive 是「演绎的」（第 1 个义项：从一般规则推出个案结论）；句意：这位侦探的方法是演绎式的：他从一条通则出发，逐步缩小到一名嫌疑人。图中可辨识物件：多米诺骨牌、放大镜、嫌疑人照片、推理板、红色连线。

pos.zh: 演绎的；推论的；运用演绎法的

derivatives.zh: 演绎主义（认为演绎是主要知识方法）

senses.title: From general to particular
senses.titleCN: 从一般到个别：由通则落到个案
senses.definition: reasoning that starts from general premises and derives a particular conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从一般前提出发推出特定结论的推理
senses.example: The detective's method was deductive: he began with a general rule and narrowed it to one suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 这位侦探的方法是演绎式的：他从一条通则出发，逐步缩小到一名嫌疑人。
senses.why: deducere means 'to lead down'. Deductive reasoning leads a conclusion down from a wide premise to a narrow case, like water channelled from a broad basin into one cup.
senses.whyCN: deducere 意为“引下”。演绎推理把结论从宽泛前提引到狭窄个案，如同水从宽盆引入一只杯子。

senses.title: The deductive method
senses.titleCN: 演绎法：作为研究路径的演绎
senses.definition: a research approach that begins with theory and derives testable predictions
senses.definitionCN: 以理论为起点、推出可检验预测的研究路径
senses.example: The study follows a deductive method, testing hypotheses drawn from theory.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究采用演绎法，检验由理论推出的假设。
senses.why: A method is reasoning made repeatable: the researcher fixes the general premises first, then leads each prediction down in a stated order.
senses.whyCN: 方法使推理可重复：研究者先固定一般前提，再按既定顺序把每个预测引下来。

senses.title: A deductive argument
senses.titleCN: 演绎论证：前提为真则结论必真
senses.definition: an argument whose conclusion follows necessarily from its premises
senses.definitionCN: 结论必然由前提推出的论证
senses.example: A deductive argument can be valid even when its premises are false.
senses.exampleCN: 演绎论证即使前提为假，也可以是有效的。
senses.why: The downward chain is tight: if the premises hold, the conclusion cannot escape. Validity concerns that link, not the truth of the starting points.
senses.whyCN: 这条向下的链条很紧：前提若成立，结论就逃不掉。有效性关乎这一联系，而非起点的真假。

senses.title: Hypothetico-deductive science
senses.titleCN: 假说—演绎：先提假设再推可测结果
senses.definition: describing the scientific pattern in which a hypothesis is proposed and consequences are deduced and tested
senses.definitionCN: 指提出假设、推出后果并加以检验的科学模式
senses.example: The hypothetico-deductive model treats prediction as the test of theory.
senses.exampleCN: 假说—演绎模型把预测当作理论的检验。
senses.why: Science borrows the downward chain twice: first from theory to hypothesis, then from hypothesis to an observable prediction that can fail.
senses.whyCN: 科学两次借用这条向下链条：先从理论到假说，再从假说到可失败的可观测预测。

senses.title: Mathematical proof
senses.titleCN: 数学证明：从公理推到定理
senses.definition: in mathematics, proceeding from axioms or definitions by necessary steps to a theorem
senses.definitionCN: 数学中从公理或定义经必然步骤推到定理
senses.example: The theorem is established by a deductive proof from three axioms.
senses.exampleCN: 该定理由三条公理经演绎证明确立。
senses.why: Mathematics is the home of the pure chain: each step is forced by the one above, with no empirical gap, which is why deductive is strongest there.
senses.whyCN: 数学是纯链条的故乡：每一步都被上一步逼出，没有经验缺口，因此 deductive 在此最强。

senses.title: Deductive closure in epistemology
senses.titleCN: 演绎闭合：已知前提必带出结论
senses.definition: in epistemology, the principle that if one knows a proposition and deduces a consequence, one can know that consequence
senses.definitionCN: 认识论原则：若知道某命题并由之演绎出后果，则也可知道该后果
senses.example: Deductive closure explains why knowledge can extend by inference.
senses.exampleCN: 演绎闭合解释了知识为何能通过推理扩展。
senses.why: If the chain is necessary, then whoever holds the top link holds the bottom one too. Epistemology turns that image into a principle about what a knower may claim.
senses.whyCN: 若链条是必然的，那么握住上端的人也就握住下端。认识论把这个意象变成关于认识者可以主张什么的原则。

senses.title: Detective-style inference
senses.titleCN: 侦探式推断：由线索收窄到唯一
senses.definition: in everyday usage, describing the process of narrowing possibilities by eliminating alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中指通过排除其他可能来收窄答案的过程
senses.example: His deductive skills eliminated every suspect but one.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演绎能力排除了除一人之外的所有嫌疑人。
senses.why: Popular writing uses deductive for any neat narrowing, even when the reasoning is really probabilistic. The strict sense requires entailment, not just elimination.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作把 deductive 用于任何漂亮的收窄，即使推理其实是概率性的。严格义要求蕴含，而不只是排除。

senses.title: The deductive-nomological model
senses.titleCN: 演绎—律则模型：用定律解释事件
senses.definition: in philosophy of science, describing an explanation in which an event is deduced from general laws and initial conditions
senses.definitionCN: 科学哲学中指从一般定律与初始条件演绎出事件以作解释
senses.example: The deductive-nomological model places the law at the top of the chain.
senses.exampleCN: 演绎—律则模型把定律放在链条顶端。
senses.why: Explanation becomes deduction: the event is the last domino, and the laws plus initial conditions are the earlier ones that make its fall necessary.
senses.whyCN: 解释变成演绎：事件是最后一张骨牌，定律与初始条件是使之必然倒下的前面那些牌。

intro.en: Deductive is deduct + -ive, built on Latin deducere 'to lead away or down'. It names the direction of reasoning rather than the content.
intro.cn: deductive 是 deduct + -ive，建立在拉丁 deducere“引开、引下”上。它命名的是推理的方向，而非内容。

items.en: deducere 'to lead down or away' combines de- 'down, away' with ducere 'to lead'. The physical image is escorting something from a higher or larger place to a lower or narrower one.
items.cn: deducere“引下、引开”由 de-“向下、离开”与 ducere“引导”组成。其物理意象是把某物从较高或较大处引到较低或较窄处。

items.en: Medieval logicians used the Latin stem for drawing a conclusion from premises. English deduction and deductive entered learned prose in the 16th and 17th centuries.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学家用这个拉丁词干表示从前提引出结论。英语 deduction 与 deductive 在16、17世纪进入学术文本。

items.en: The suffix -ive, Latin -ivus, marks a tendency or nature: deductive describes reasoning that has the nature of leading a conclusion down.
items.cn: 后缀 -ive（拉丁 -ivus）标记倾向或性质：deductive 描述具有“把结论引下”性质的推理。

items.en: By the 19th century deductive was fixed in the pair deductive / inductive, naming opposite directions of inquiry.
items.cn: 到19世纪，deductive 已固定于 deductive／inductive 这一对术语中，命名相反的探究方向。

items.en: The 20th century added hypothetico-deductive method and the deductive-nomological model, both extending the downward chain into accounts of scientific practice.
items.cn: 20世纪新增 hypothetico-deductive method 与 deductive-nomological model，把向下链条延伸到对科学实践的说明。

items.en: Whether English deductive came directly from Latin deductivus or was newly formed on deduction is uncertain. The deeper origin of ducere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 英语 deductive 是直接来自拉丁 deductivus，还是在 deduction 上重新构造，存疑。ducere 的更深来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains forms of the same family with different jobs; the second contains reasoning terms that move in a different direction.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中功能不同的形式；第二组是方向不同的推理术语。

entries.definition: The process or result of deductive reasoning, or an amount subtracted; the noun, not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 演绎推理的过程或结果，或扣除额；是名词而非形容词。

entries.definition: Capable of being inferred; it describes a conclusion, not a method.
entries.definitionCN: 可被推断出来的；描述结论，而非方法。

entries.definition: Tending to bring about a result, as in conducive to health. It shares ducere but leads toward an effect, not down from premises.
entries.definitionCN: 有助于产生某结果的，如 conducive to health。它共享 ducere，但方向是引向效果，而非从前提引下。

entries.definition: Relating to inference of any kind; it covers deduction and induction, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何推理有关的；覆盖演绎与归纳，因此更宽。

entries.definition: Reasoning from particular observations to a general rule; the mirror image of deductive.
entries.definitionCN: 从个别观察推出一般规则；是 deductive 的镜像方向。

entries.definition: Relating to the syllogism, a specific two-premise deductive form; narrower than deductive.
entries.definitionCN: 与三段论这一特定双前提演绎形式有关；比 deductive 更窄。

entries.definition: Known independently of experience; deductive reasoning is often a priori, but the terms are not equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 不依赖经验而知的；演绎推理常是先验的，但两个术语并不等同。

entries.definition: Serving to prove or show clearly; it stresses the force of proof rather than the direction of reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于证明或清楚展示的；强调证明力度，而非推理方向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: genuine morphology, fixed collocations and the ducere word family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、固定搭配与 ducere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'down' + ducere 'lead' + -ive: an adjective for reasoning that leads a conclusion down from a premise.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ ducere“引导”+ -ive：描述把结论从前提引下的推理的形容词。

normal.en: The pair deductive / inductive is a direction pair: down from the general versus up from the particular.
normal.cn: deductive／inductive 是方向对：从一般向下，从个别向上。

normal.en: Learn deductive reasoning, deductive argument and deductive method; these are the standard academic phrases.
normal.cn: 记住 deductive reasoning、deductive argument、deductive method；这些是标准学术短语。

normal.en: deduction, deduce, deduct, deductive and deductively all carry the duc- core.
normal.cn: deduction、deduce、deduct、deductive、deductively 都带有 duc- 核心。

normal.en: Do not confuse deductive with deducible: one is a method, the other says a conclusion can be drawn.
normal.cn: 不要把 deductive 与 deducible 混淆：一个是方法，一个说结论可被推出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dominoes starting from a broad base block and ending at one small tile.
abstract.cn: 想象一排多米诺骨牌从宽大的底座开始，到一张小牌结束。

abstract.en: Picture a funnel: many general possibilities pour in at the top, one case comes out at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只漏斗：许多一般可能性从上方灌入，底部只流出一个个案。

abstract.en: Picture a locked chain where pulling the top link necessarily moves the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一条锁紧的链：拉动最上一环，最后一环必然跟着动。

examples.en: Deductive reasoning moves from a general rule to a specific case.
examples.cn: 演绎推理从一般规则推进到具体个案。

examples.en: The proof is deductive: each step follows necessarily from the previous one.
examples.cn: 这个证明是演绎性的：每一步都必然由前一步推出。

examples.en: Her deductive approach began with theory and ended with a testable prediction.
examples.cn: 她的演绎路径从理论出发，最终得出可检验的预测。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（下）+ duct（管道）+ ive”——像管道一样把结论从上往下输送 → deductive 演绎的、推论的

root: 拉丁 deducere“引下、引开”（de-“向下／离开”+ ducere“引导”）；deduct- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one direction: downward from the general. The chain may run from premises to a case, from theory to a prediction, from axioms to a theorem, or from laws to an event.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个方向：从一般向下。链条可以从前提跑到个案、从理论跑到预测、从公理跑到定理，或从定律跑到事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of dominoes falling from a wide base to one small tile.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排骨牌从宽底座倒向一张小牌。

branches.en: CORE LOGIC: leading a conclusion down from a general rule to a single case.
branches.cn: 核心逻辑：把结论从通则引到个案的过程。

branches.en: RESEARCH: the deductive method and the hypothetico-deductive pattern both start with theory and derive something testable.
branches.cn: 研究：演绎法与假说—演绎模式都从理论出发，推出可检验之物。

branches.en: PROOF AND EXPLANATION: a mathematical proof and a deductive-nomological explanation both make the last step unavoidable.
branches.cn: 证明与解释：数学证明与演绎—律则解释，都使最后一步不可避免。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND DETECTION: deductive closure extends what a knower may claim; detective-style inference narrows suspects.
branches.cn: 知识与侦破：演绎闭合扩展认识者可主张的范围；侦探式推断收窄嫌疑人。

branches.en: VALIDITY: the form matters more than the truth of the premises, which is why a valid deduction can start from falsehoods.
branches.cn: 有效性：形式比前提真假更重要，因此有效演绎可以从假前提出发。

intro.en: Deductive is deduct + -ive, on the Latin participle stem. The suffix marks the nature of the reasoning, while the prefix de- and root duc- are no longer separable in English.
intro.cn: deductive 是 deduct + -ive，建立在拉丁分词词干上。后缀标记推理的性质，而前缀 de- 与词根 duc- 在英语中已不可再分。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'to lead' gives a family that includes conduct, induce, reduce, produce, introduce, education and deduct. Each prefixed form specifies a direction, which is why the family is easy to map.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”衍生出 conduct、induce、reduce、produce、introduce、education、deduct 等词族。每个带前缀形式都指定方向，因此这个词族容易画成地图。

items.meaningCN: 从一般到个别的演绎推理（-ive 表性质）
items.example: The course teaches deductive and inductive logic.
items.exampleCN: 这门课教授演绎逻辑与归纳逻辑。

items.meaning: the act or result of deducing; a subtraction
items.meaningCN: 演绎；推论；扣除（-ion 表行为或结果）
items.example: The deduction is valid but unsound.
items.exampleCN: 这个演绎有效但不可靠（前提不真）。

items.meaningCN: 推断；演绎（de-“向下”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: From the map we deduced the old boundary.
items.exampleCN: 我们从地图推断出旧边界。

items.meaningCN: 扣除；减去
items.example: Tax is deducted before the salary is paid.
items.exampleCN: 税款在发薪前扣除。

items.meaningCN: 以演绎方式（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The conclusion was reached deductively.
items.exampleCN: 该结论是以演绎方式得出的。

items.meaning: the view that deduction is the main route to knowledge
items.meaningCN: 演绎主义：认为演绎是主要知识路径（-ism 表主义）
items.example: Deductivism overstates the role of axioms.
items.exampleCN: 演绎主义夸大了公理的作用。

items.meaning: to lead into; to infer a general rule
items.meaningCN: 诱导；归纳（in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: They induced a rule from repeated observations.
items.exampleCN: 他们从反复观察中归纳出一条规则。

items.meaningCN: 减少（re-“回”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The model reduces the problem to two variables.
items.exampleCN: 该模型把问题化简为两个变量。

items.meaning: to lead, guide, or carry out
items.meaningCN: 引导；进行（con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The team conducted the trial in three hospitals.
items.exampleCN: 团队在三家医院开展了试验。

latinEntries.meaning: serving to lead out or infer (Medieval Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用于引出或推断的（中世纪拉丁）

latinEntries.meaning: a leading away; a drawing out

definition_en: a lack or shortage of something needed, or a fault that makes something incomplete
core_image: 木桶侧壁缺了一块，水位低于刻度线
scene: Iron deficiency is common among children in the region.
sceneCN: 这里 deficiency 是「缺乏」（第 2 个义项：营养素摄入不足）；句意：该地区儿童缺铁很常见。图中可辨识物件：木桶缺口、低于刻度的水位、血检报告、铁剂药瓶、儿童身高尺。

pos.zh: 缺乏；不足；缺陷；（账目）不足额

senses.title: A lack of something needed
senses.titleCN: 缺乏：缺了必需的东西
senses.definition: the state of not having enough of something that is necessary
senses.definitionCN: 必需之物数量不足的状态
senses.example: The report identifies a deficiency of trained staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出受训人员不足。
senses.why: Latin deficere means 'to fail or be lacking', from de- 'away' and facere 'to do'. Something is missing, so the job cannot be done, and the noun names that gap.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 deficere 意为“失败、缺少”，由 de-“离开”与 facere“做”构成。某物缺失，事情就做不成，名词命名的正是这个缺口。

senses.title: A nutrient deficiency
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏：身体缺某种养分
senses.definition: a shortage of a nutrient required for health
senses.definitionCN: 健康所需的某种营养素不足
senses.example: Iron deficiency is common among children in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区儿童缺铁很常见。
senses.why: The body is a system that needs inputs; when one input falls below the needed level, the gap is named by the nutrient that is missing.
senses.whyCN: 身体是需要输入的系统；当某项输入低于所需水平，缺口就用缺失的那种营养素来命名。

senses.title: Immune deficiency
senses.titleCN: 免疫缺陷：防线缺了一块
senses.definition: a weakness or absence in the body's immune defences
senses.definitionCN: 身体免疫防线的薄弱或缺失
senses.example: The treatment is designed for patients with immune deficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 该疗法专为免疫缺陷患者设计。
senses.why: The 'gap in the wall' image becomes medical: a missing part of the defence lets infection in, so the deficiency is a structural hole rather than a low number.
senses.whyCN: “墙上的缺口”意象进入医学：防线缺一部分，感染便能进入，因此缺陷是结构性的洞，而不只是数值偏低。

senses.title: A defect in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：设计或系统里的毛病
senses.definition: a fault or weakness that makes something incomplete or ineffective
senses.definitionCN: 使某物不完整或失效的缺点或薄弱处
senses.example: The audit found a deficiency in the control system.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现控制系统中存在缺陷。
senses.why: Deficiency can point to a missing part rather than a missing quantity: the thing is not merely low on stock, it lacks a piece it needs to work.
senses.whyCN: deficiency 也可指缺了一个部件，而非数量不足：该物不只是存量少，而是缺少工作所需的零件。

senses.title: A deficiency judgment
senses.titleCN: 不足额判决：拍卖款不够还债
senses.definition: in law, a judgment ordering a debtor to pay the balance left after property is sold
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指财产变卖后仍欠余额、判令债务人补足的判决
senses.example: The bank obtained a deficiency judgment for the remaining balance.
senses.exampleCN: 银行就剩余余额获得了不足额判决。
senses.why: Foreclosure recovers part of a debt; the rest is still missing. The legal phrase names the gap that the court orders the debtor to close.
senses.whyCN: 止赎只能收回部分债务，其余仍然缺失。这个法律短语命名的正是法院命令债务人补上的缺口。

senses.title: A revenue shortfall
senses.titleCN: 收入缺口：预算没凑够
senses.definition: an amount by which income falls short of what is needed or expected
senses.definitionCN: 收入低于所需或预期数额的差额
senses.example: The city faces a budget deficiency of ten million dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 该市面临一千万美元的预算缺口。
senses.why: Accounts compare what should be there with what is there. The difference is a hole in the total, and deficiency names it more formally than shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 账目把应有的数额与实际数额相比。差额就是总数上的洞，deficiency 比 shortfall 更正式地命名它。

senses.title: An audit finding
senses.titleCN: 审计缺陷：内控上的可报告问题
senses.definition: in auditing, a weakness in internal controls serious enough to be reported
senses.definitionCN: 审计中严重到需要报告内部控制薄弱之处
senses.example: The auditors listed two material deficiencies in reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师列出了报告方面的两项重大缺陷。
senses.why: Audit language treats a missing control as a gap through which error can pass. The word is technical because the gap is defined by a standard, not by a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 审计语言把缺失的控制视为让错误穿过的缺口。这个词之所以技术化，是因为缺口由标准界定，而非凭感觉。

senses.title: A deficiency disease
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏病：缺某物直接致病
senses.definition: a disease caused by the absence of a specific nutrient
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少特定营养素而直接引起的疾病
senses.example: Scurvy is a classic deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin C.
senses.exampleCN: 坏血病是缺乏维生素 C 引起的典型营养缺乏病。
senses.why: The compound joins the gap to its consequence: remove one necessary input and the body fails in a recognizable pattern, which medicine names after the missing item.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把缺口与后果连起来：去掉一项必需输入，身体就以可识别的方式衰竭，医学便以缺失物来命名疾病。

intro.en: Deficiency is deficient + -cy, from Latin deficientia, built on deficere 'to fail, be lacking'. The same verb gives deficit and defect.
intro.cn: deficiency 是 deficient + -cy，来自拉丁 deficientia，建立在 deficere“失败、缺少”上。同一动词还产生 deficit 与 defect。

items.en: deficere 'to fail, run short, desert' combines de- 'away' and facere 'to do, make'. The picture is something withdrawing from where it is needed, so the task is left undone.
items.cn: deficere“失败、短缺、背离”由 de-“离开”与 facere“做、造”组成。画面是某物从需要它的地方撤走，任务便无法完成。

items.en: deficientia 'a failing, a lack' is the abstract noun. English forms deficiency with the French-Latin ending -cy, as in other -cy nouns.
items.cn: deficientia“失败、缺乏”是抽象名词。英语用法语—拉丁来源的 -cy 词尾构成 deficiency，与其他 -cy 名词一致。

items.en: English deficiency is recorded from the 17th century in medical and administrative writing. The exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 deficiency 在17世纪的医学与行政文本中已有记录。最早确切年代为约数。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries fixed deficiency disease and nutrient deficiency as medicine learned to identify specific missing substances.
items.cn: 19、20世纪，随着医学学会识别具体缺失物质，deficiency disease 与 nutrient deficiency 固定下来。

items.en: Deficiency judgment and budget deficiency extend the word to money: the amount by which a fund or payment falls short of what is owed.
items.cn: deficiency judgment 与 budget deficiency 把这个词延伸到金钱：资金或付款低于应付数额的差额。

items.en: The exact semantic path from 'failing' to 'structural defect' is not fully documented. The deeper PIE origin of facere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 从“失败”到“结构缺陷”的确切语义路径没有完整记录。facere 的更早印欧语来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains the same-root nouns that are often confused in finance and law; the second contains shortage words with different scopes.
note.cn: 第一组是同根名词，在金融与法律语境中常被混淆；第二组是范围不同的“短缺”类词。

entries.definition: The amount by which spending exceeds income; it is usually a financial figure, while deficiency can also be a defect or a nutrient lack.
entries.definitionCN: 支出超过收入的差额；通常是财务数字，而 deficiency 也可指缺陷或营养缺乏。

entries.definition: A fault that makes a product or plan imperfect; it is countable and concrete, closer to sense 4.
entries.definitionCN: 使产品或计划不完美的毛病；可数且具体，更接近第 4 个义项。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'lacking'; deficiency is the noun for the lack itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“缺乏的”的形容词；deficiency 是“缺乏”本身的名词。

entries.definition: A situation in which supply is below demand; it is usually temporary and economic.
entries.definitionCN: 供应低于需求的情形；通常为暂时的经济现象。

entries.definition: The absence of something; the most general word, without the technical or medical frame.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不存在；最通用的词，没有技术或医学框架。

entries.definition: The amount by which a target is missed; it names a figure, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 未达到目标的差额；命名的是一个数字，而非状态。

entries.definition: The quality of being insufficient for a purpose; it often carries a judgment of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对某用途而言不够的性质；常带质量判断。

entries.definition: A point that can be attacked or can fail; it is broader than a technical deficiency.
entries.definitionCN: 可被攻击或可能失效的点；比技术意义上的 deficiency 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, standard collocations and the deficere family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、标准搭配与 deficere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'away' + facere 'do': something has gone away, so the work cannot be done — that is the lack.
normal.cn: de-“离开”+ facere“做”：某物离开了，事情就做不成——这就是缺乏。

normal.en: deficiency, deficit and defect are siblings: a lack, its amount, and the fault it leaves behind.
normal.cn: deficiency、deficit、defect 是同胞词：缺乏、差额、以及留下的毛病。

normal.en: Learn nutrient deficiency, immune deficiency and deficiency disease; these are the medical core.
normal.cn: 记住 nutrient deficiency、immune deficiency、deficiency disease；这些是医学核心搭配。

normal.en: In finance use deficit for the shortfall; in medicine use deficiency for the missing substance.
normal.cn: 财务缺口用 deficit；医学缺失用 deficiency。

normal.en: deficient is the adjective, deficiency the noun, deficiently the adverb.
normal.cn: deficient 是形容词，deficiency 是名词，deficiently 是副词。

abstract.en: Picture a barrel with one plank missing, so the water line can never reach the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶少了一块板，水位线永远到不了刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with one brick pulled out, leaving a gap wide enough for a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上被抽走一块砖，留下一个能伸进手的缺口。

abstract.en: Picture an invoice where the paid amount stops short of the total, leaving a visible balance line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张发票，已付金额没到总额，留下一行清晰的余额。

examples.en: Vitamin D deficiency can weaken the bones over time.
examples.cn: 维生素 D 缺乏会随着时间使骨骼变弱。

examples.en: The review found serious deficiencies in the safety procedures.
examples.cn: 审查发现安全程序存在严重缺陷。

examples.en: The fund was set up to cover a deficiency in local services.
examples.cn: 该基金旨在弥补地方服务的不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（低）+ fic（做）+ iency”——该做的没做到位，桶就缺一块 → deficiency 缺乏、缺陷

root: 拉丁 deficere“失败、缺少”（de-“离开”+ facere“做”）；deficient + -cy 名词后缀，同根词有 deficit、defect。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gap: something needed is not there. The gap may be a nutrient, a defence, a control, a payment or a whole missing part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个缺口：需要的东西不在。缺口可以是营养、防线、控制、付款，或整个缺失的部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a missing plank in a barrel, with the water line below the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桶少了一块板，水位低于刻度。

branches.en: DEFECT: a missing part is the same gap measured in structure.
branches.cn: 缺陷：缺失的部件，是缺口在结构层面的度量。

branches.en: BODY: a nutrient below the needed level and an immune defence with a hole both let the system fail.
branches.cn: 身体：营养素低于所需水平、免疫防线有洞，都会让系统失效。

branches.en: MONEY: a deficiency judgment and a budget gap both name the balance that is still missing.
branches.cn: 金钱：不足额判决与预算缺口，都命名仍然缺失的余额。

branches.en: TECHNICAL CONSEQUENCES: an audit deficiency is a missing control; a deficiency disease is the body's failure from a missing nutrient.
branches.cn: 技术后果：审计缺陷是缺失的控制；营养缺乏病是身体因缺营养素而衰竭。

branches.en: GENERAL CORE: the plain sense covers every specialised branch, since each branch is a particular kind of 'not enough'.
branches.cn: 一般核心：平实义覆盖所有专业分支，因为每个分支都是“不够”的某种具体形态。

intro.en: Deficiency is deficient + -cy. The suffix forms abstract nouns of state; the base is the Latin verb deficere, whose de- and fac- are fossilized.
intro.cn: deficiency 是 deficient + -cy。后缀构成状态抽象名词；词基是拉丁动词 deficere，其 de- 与 fac- 已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do, make' underlies a huge family: efficient, sufficient, deficient, defect, factory, fiction and fashion. The prefix changes whether the doing succeeds or falls short.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere“做、造”支撑着一个庞大词族：efficient、sufficient、deficient、defect、factory、fiction、fashion。前缀决定“做”是成功还是不足。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏；缺陷（-cy 状态名词）
items.example: The deficiency was corrected by adding a supplement.
items.exampleCN: 通过补充剂纠正了这一缺乏。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏的；不足的（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: The diet was deficient in calcium.
items.exampleCN: 这种饮食缺钙。

items.meaning: the amount by which something falls short
items.meaningCN: 赤字；不足额（-it 分词词尾）
items.example: The budget deficit grew for a third year.
items.exampleCN: 预算赤字连续第三年扩大。

items.meaningCN: 缺陷；瑕疵（de-“离开”+ fect-“被造”）
items.example: The defect appeared after two weeks of use.
items.exampleCN: 使用两周后出现了缺陷。

items.meaningCN: 不足地；有缺陷地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The system performed deficiently under load.
items.exampleCN: 系统在负载下表现不足。

items.meaningCN: 高效的（ex-“出”+ fic-“做”+ -ient）
items.example: The new engine is more efficient.
items.exampleCN: 新引擎效率更高。

items.meaningCN: 充足的（sub-“向上”+ fic-“做”+ -ient）
items.example: The evidence was sufficient for a verdict.
items.exampleCN: 证据足以作出裁决。

items.meaning: a place where goods are made
items.meaningCN: 工厂（fact-“做”+ -ory 表场所）
items.example: The factory produces parts for turbines.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产涡轮零件。

items.meaningCN: 虚构；小说（fict-“塑造、编造”+ -ion）
items.example: The novel mixes fiction with recorded history.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说把虚构与有记载的历史混合在一起。

definition_zh: 缺乏的；不足的；有缺陷的
definition_en: lacking something necessary, or falling short of a required standard
core_image: 一只碗底有洞，汤从洞里漏走
scene: The soil is deficient in nitrogen, so the crops grow slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 deficient 是「缺乏的」（第 1 个义项：缺少必需成分）；句意：这片土壤缺氮，所以作物长得慢。图中可辨识物件：缺口的碗、土壤剖面、枯黄作物、氮肥袋、检测试纸。

pos.zh: 缺乏的；不足的；有缺陷的（常与 in 连用）

senses.title: Lacking an essential element
senses.titleCN: 缺乏必需成分：缺少关键的那一样
senses.definition: not having enough of a substance or quality that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 所需物质或品质的数量不足
senses.example: The soil is deficient in nitrogen, so the crops grow slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土壤缺氮，所以作物长得慢。
senses.why: deficere is 'to be lacking'. The adjective describes a thing whose needed part has withdrawn, so it cannot perform its function fully.
senses.whyCN: deficere 意为“缺少”。这个形容词描述某物所需的部分已撤走，因此无法充分发挥作用。

senses.title: Insufficient in quantity
senses.titleCN: 数量不足：够用线以下
senses.definition: existing in an amount too small for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 数量太少、不足以满足用途
senses.example: The supply of trained nurses is deficient in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 农村地区受训护士的供给不足。
senses.why: Here the lack is numeric: the stock is below the line the task requires, so the adjective answers 'how much' rather than 'what part'.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺乏是数值性的：存量低于任务要求的线，因此形容词回答的是“多少”，而非“缺哪部分”。

senses.title: Below a required standard
senses.titleCN: 不达标：没到规定的水平
senses.definition: falling short of a standard set by a rule, contract or examiner
senses.definitionCN: 低于规则、合同或考核者设定的标准
senses.example: The service was judged deficient in three areas.
senses.exampleCN: 该服务在三个方面被判定不达标。
senses.why: A standard draws a line, and deficiency is the space below it. The adjective turns a comparison into an official verdict.
senses.whyCN: 标准画出一条线，deficient 就是线下的空间。这个形容词把比较变成正式判定。

senses.title: Defective or incomplete
senses.titleCN: 有缺陷的：缺了部件，运转不全
senses.definition: having a fault or missing part that prevents full working
senses.definitionCN: 存在妨碍完整运作的毛病或缺失部件
senses.example: The model is deficient because it ignores feedback.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型有缺陷，因为它忽略了反馈。
senses.why: The gap here is structural rather than quantitative: something needed for the whole to work is absent, so the object is incomplete, not merely low.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺口是结构性的而非数量性的：整体运作所需之物缺席，因此该物不完整，而不只是数量低。

senses.title: Nutritionally inadequate
senses.titleCN: 营养不足的：饮食里缺东西
senses.definition: of a diet, lacking the nutrients needed for health
senses.definitionCN: 指饮食缺少健康所需的营养素
senses.example: A deficient diet can cause stunted growth.
senses.exampleCN: 营养不足的饮食会导致生长迟缓。
senses.why: The body needs a set of inputs; a diet missing one of them is deficient in that item, and the medical phrase keeps the preposition in.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要一组输入；缺少其中一项的饮食就在该项上 deficient，医学短语保留介词 in。

senses.title: Academically behind
senses.titleCN: 学业不达标：某项能力没跟上
senses.definition: in education, performing below the expected level in a subject or skill
senses.definitionCN: 教育中在某学科或技能上低于预期水平
senses.example: Students who are deficient in reading need extra support.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读能力不足的学生需要额外支持。
senses.why: Schools measure a skill against a grade-level line; deficiency names the distance below that line without saying the student cannot learn.
senses.whyCN: 学校按年级水平线衡量技能；deficiency 命名低于该线的距离，并不表示学生学不会。

senses.title: A dated clinical label
senses.titleCN: 旧称“智力缺陷”：现已应避免
senses.definition: an outdated and offensive label formerly applied to people with intellectual disabilities
senses.definitionCN: 旧时加于智力障碍者的过时且冒犯性标签
senses.example: The phrase 'mentally deficient' is now avoided in clinical writing.
senses.exampleCN: 如今临床写作中已避免使用 mentally deficient 这一说法。
senses.why: The word's logic is the same gap image, but applying it to a person turns a description of need into a label. Modern usage replaces it with person-first terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的逻辑仍是同一缺口意象，但把它用在人身上，就把对需要的描述变成了标签。现代用法以“人优先”的术语取代它。

senses.title: A deficient number
senses.titleCN: 亏数：真因数和小于本身
senses.definition: in number theory, a number whose proper divisors add up to less than the number itself
senses.definitionCN: 数论中真因数之和小于该数本身的数
senses.example: Eight is a deficient number because 1+2+4 is less than 8.
senses.exampleCN: 八是亏数，因为 1+2+4 小于 8。
senses.why: Mathematics turns 'falls short' into an exact definition: the sum of the parts is deficient, that is, less than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 数学把“不足”变成精确定义：各部分之和 deficient，即小于整体。

intro.en: Deficient is the adjective from Latin deficere, present participle stem deficient-. It shares a root with deficiency, deficit and defect.
intro.cn: deficient 是拉丁 deficere 的形容词，来自现在分词词干 deficient-。它与 deficiency、deficit、defect 共享词根。

items.en: deficere 'to fail, be lacking' is de- 'away' plus facere 'to do'. The image is a worker or supply stepping away from the task, leaving it unfinished.
items.cn: deficere“失败、缺少”是 de-“离开”加 facere“做”。画面是工人或供给从任务旁走开，留下未完成的工作。

items.en: The present participle deficiens 'lacking' supplies the stem deficient-, which English uses unchanged in the adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 deficiens“缺少的”提供词干 deficient-，英语形容词原样使用这一词干。

items.en: English deficient appears in the 16th century, mainly in medical and scholarly descriptions of what a body, diet or argument lacks.
items.cn: 英语 deficient 于16世纪出现，主要用于医学与学术文本，描述身体、饮食或论证缺少什么。

items.en: The construction deficient in plus a noun became fixed, parallel to rich in and weak in. It names the dimension of the lack.
items.cn: deficient in + 名词的结构固定下来，与 rich in、weak in 平行。它命名缺乏的维度。

items.en: Education, law and mathematics each adopted the adjective for their own standards, from grade-level performance to deficient numbers.
items.cn: 教育、法律与数学各自采用这个形容词来表示自己的标准，从年级表现到亏数。

items.en: The exact first English use is uncertain, and the deeper origin of facere is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 最早的确切英语用例存疑，facere 的更深来源属重构而非有据可查。

note.en: The first group is the same-root set that learners mix up; the second contains adjectives of shortage with different implications.
note.cn: 第一组是学习者常混淆的同根词；第二组是含义侧重不同的“不足”形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the lack or defect; deficient is the adjective describing the thing that lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺乏或缺陷的名词；deficient 是描述该物缺少什么的形容词。

entries.definition: A financial shortfall; it is a countable amount, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 财务缺口；是可数金额，不是形容词。

entries.definition: Having a fault that makes something unusable; it stresses malfunction, while deficient can mean simply too little.
entries.definitionCN: 有使某物不可用的毛病；强调功能故障，而 deficient 可仅指数量太少。

entries.definition: Not having something; the most general word and the least technical.
entries.definitionCN: 不具有某物；最通用、最不技术化。

entries.definition: Not enough for a purpose, often with a quality judgment; broader than deficient in a specific nutrient.
entries.definitionCN: 对某用途不够，常含质量判断；比“缺某种营养素”的 deficient 更宽。

entries.definition: Not enough in amount; it measures quantity, while deficient can also point to a missing part.
entries.definitionCN: 数量不够；衡量数量，而 deficient 也可指缺部件。

entries.definition: Not reaching a required amount or distance; it is plainer and often used of money or time.
entries.definitionCN: 未达到所需数量或距离；更平实，常用于钱或时间。

entries.definition: Available only in small amounts relative to demand; it describes supply conditions, not a thing's own make-up.
entries.definitionCN: 相对需求而言供应量很小；描述供应状况，而非某物自身构成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, the in-pattern and the facere family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、in 搭配与 facere 词族。

normal.en: deficient in: the preposition names the exact dimension that is missing.
normal.cn: deficient in：介词指出缺失的具体维度。

normal.en: deficere 'fail to do': the thing could not do its job because a needed part stepped away.
normal.cn: deficere“没做成”：所需的部分走开了，这东西就无法完成工作。

normal.en: Learn deficient in, nutritionally deficient and deficient number; they mark the general, medical and mathematical branches.
normal.cn: 记住 deficient in、nutritionally deficient、deficient number；分别标记一般、医学与数学分支。

normal.en: deficiency is the noun, deficient the adjective, deficiently the adverb.
normal.cn: deficiency 是名词，deficient 是形容词，deficiently 是副词。

normal.en: Avoid the dated phrase mentally deficient; use person-first language about intellectual disability.
normal.cn: 避免旧说法 mentally deficient；谈智力障碍时使用“人优先”的表达。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl with a hole in the bottom, so no amount of soup can stay at the right level.
abstract.cn: 想象碗底有个洞，无论加多少汤都到不了应有的高度。

abstract.en: Picture a chair missing one leg, standing but unable to bear weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把缺了一条腿的椅子，立着却承不了重。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge needle that cannot reach the green zone, always stopping short.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表指针总也到不了绿色区域，永远差一截。

examples.en: The report says the bridge is structurally deficient.
examples.cn: 报告称这座桥在结构上存在缺陷。

examples.en: Children on a deficient diet are more likely to fall ill.
examples.cn: 饮食营养不足的儿童更容易生病。

examples.en: The evidence was deficient, so the case was dismissed.
examples.cn: 证据不足，因此案件被驳回。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（低）+ fish（鱼）+ ent”——池塘里鱼太少，低得不够吃 → deficient 缺乏的、不足的

root: 拉丁 deficere“失败、缺少”（de-“离开”+ facere“做”）；现在分词词干 deficient- + -ent 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gap: the needed item is below the line. The line may be set by a diet, a standard, a design, a classroom, a clinic or a mathematical definition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个缺口：所需之物低于标准线。这条线可由饮食、规范、设计、课堂、诊所或数学定义设定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl with a hole, so the level can never reach the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：碗底有洞，液面永远到不了刻度。

branches.en: QUANTITY: stock below the line of enough.
branches.cn: 数量：存量低于够用线。

branches.en: STANDARDS: a service judged below standard and a student below grade level are both measured against an external line.
branches.cn: 标准：服务不达标与学生低于年级水平，都以外部标准线衡量。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND LABEL: a model missing feedback is incomplete; the dated clinical label shows what happens when a gap is attached to a person.
branches.cn: 结构与标签：忽略反馈的模型不完整；过时的临床标签显示，把缺口贴到人身上会发生什么。

branches.en: MEDICINE AND MATHEMATICS: a deficient diet lacks an input; a deficient number has parts summing below the whole.
branches.cn: 医学与数学：营养不足的饮食缺输入；亏数的各部分之和小于整体。

branches.en: GENERAL CORE: every branch is a specific way of being below what is needed.
branches.cn: 一般核心：每个分支都是“低于所需”的一种具体方式。

intro.en: Deficient is a Latin present-participle adjective in -ent. The base verb deficere is fossilized, but the suffix -ent remains recognizable as an adjective ending.
intro.cn: deficient 是拉丁现在分词形容词，词尾 -ent。词基动词 deficere 已凝固，但 -ent 仍可识别为形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do, make' underlies efficient, sufficient, deficient, defect, factory and fiction. The prefixes ex-, sub- and de- mark whether the doing comes out, measures up, or falls away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere“做、造”支撑 efficient、sufficient、deficient、defect、factory、fiction。前缀 ex-、sub-、de- 标记“做”是做出成果、达到要求，还是中途撤走。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏的；低于所需水平（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: The sample was deficient in two minerals.
items.exampleCN: 样本缺少两种矿物质。

items.meaning: the state or amount of lacking
items.meaningCN: 缺乏的状态或数额（-cy 状态名词）
items.example: The deficiency was measured at ten per cent.
items.exampleCN: 缺乏程度测得为百分之十。

items.meaningCN: 赤字；不足额
items.example: The deficit reached two billion.
items.exampleCN: 赤字达到二十亿。

items.meaning: a fault in what was made
items.meaningCN: 制成品上的缺陷（de-“离开”+ fect-“被造”）
items.example: The defect was found in one batch.
items.exampleCN: 缺陷在一个批次中被发现。

items.meaningCN: 不足地；不达标地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The pump worked deficiently at low pressure.
items.exampleCN: 泵在低压下工作不足。

items.meaningCN: 高效的（ex-“出”+ fic-“做”）
items.example: The process is efficient in its use of water.
items.exampleCN: 该工艺用水效率高。

items.meaningCN: 充足的（sub-“向上”+ fic-“做”）
items.example: The sample was sufficient for testing.
items.exampleCN: 样本量足以进行检测。

items.meaningCN: 工厂（fact-“造”+ -ory 表场所）
items.example: The factory runs three shifts.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂三班运转。

items.meaningCN: 虚构；小说（fict-“塑造”+ -ion）
items.example: The story is presented as fact but is fiction.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事被当作事实呈现，其实是虚构。

definition_zh: 决定性的；权威的；最终的；确定的
definition_en: authoritative and conclusive, or serving as the final and standard version of something
core_image: 一枚印章压在法律文本末尾，封住最后一行
scene: The genome sequence provided a definitive answer to the question of the species' origin.
sceneCN: 这里 definitive 是「决定性的、权威的」（第 1 个义项：足以终结争议的结论）；句意：基因组序列为该物种起源问题提供了权威答案。图中可辨识物件：印章、法律文本、DNA 双螺旋图、封蜡、签名笔。

pos.zh: 决定性的；权威的；最终的；确定的

senses.title: Conclusive and authoritative
senses.titleCN: 决定性的：足以终结争议
senses.definition: so complete and reliable that it settles a question
senses.definitionCN: 完整可靠到足以终结一个问题的
senses.example: The genome sequence provided a definitive answer to the question of the species' origin.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组序列为该物种起源问题提供了权威答案。
senses.why: definire means 'to set a boundary'. A definitive answer draws the line beyond which no further dispute can go, so it ends the question rather than merely answering it.
senses.whyCN: definire 意为“划定边界”。definitive 的答案画出界线，越过它争议无法再继续，因此它不只是回答，而是终结问题。

senses.title: The standard version
senses.titleCN: 权威版本：此后都以此为准
senses.definition: the most complete and authoritative version of a work, used as the standard
senses.definitionCN: 某作品最完整、最权威、被当作标准的版本
senses.example: The library holds the definitive edition of the letters.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆藏有这批书信的权威版本。
senses.why: An edition becomes definitive when editors have bounded the text: every known variant is judged, and the resulting version is fixed as the reference.
senses.whyCN: 当编者把文本边界划定——判断每一处已知异文，并把结果固定为参照——这个版本就成为 definitive。

senses.title: Final and legally binding
senses.titleCN: 最终且有约束力的：签下就定了
senses.definition: final and not subject to further change, as in a definitive agreement
senses.definitionCN: 最终且不可再改的，如最终协议
senses.example: The two firms signed a definitive agreement in March.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司在三月签署了最终协议。
senses.why: A boundary set in law is meant to hold. Once the agreement is definitive, later bargaining cannot move the line without a new document.
senses.whyCN: 法律上划定的边界意在固定。协议一旦成为 definitive，后来的谈判若无新文件就不能移动这条线。

senses.title: A confirmatory medical diagnosis
senses.titleCN: 确诊：不再是疑似
senses.definition: in medicine, a diagnosis established by decisive evidence rather than suspicion
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指由决定性证据确立、而非仅凭怀疑的诊断
